note: Programs marked “Checked with agency” (273 of 341) were confirmed on the agency’s or lender’s own site on that date; the rest come from current state guides and are re-checked against each agency on a rolling weekly basis. Lender grants apply only in the lender’s eligible areas. Always confirm amounts and eligibility with the program. Local lists cover each state’s largest cities and counties and can miss smaller programs; a few city websites (for example Portland, Maine) block automated checks, so also ask your city or county housing office.

national.name: Chenoa Fund
national.notes: Forgivable after 36 on-time payments; a repayable version exists for higher incomes.

national.name: National Homebuyers Fund
national.notes: Grant or 3-year forgivable loan; first-time and repeat buyers.

national.name: Chase Homebuyer Grant
national.notes: Only for homes in eligible (mostly low- and moderate-income) census tracts, with a Chase DreaMaker, standard agency, FHA or VA purchase loan. Goes first to rate buydown and fees; can’t be used for the down payment on FHA. May be reported as income.

national.name: Bank of America Down Payment Grant
national.notes: Select markets only (260+ cities and counties). Used with Bank of America’s 3%-down mortgage; no homeownership in the past 3 years; income and loan limits apply. Never repaid.

national.name: America’s Home Grant®
national.notes: Select markets only. Covers nonrecurring closing costs (title, recording) or a permanent rate buydown — not the down payment. Stacks with the Down Payment Grant for up to $17,500.

programs.name: Closing Cost Assistance Program (CCAP)
programs.notes: Can go toward down payment, closing costs or principal reduction. 3% or 4% of the loan depending on credit (tier details, incl. 640 minimum, not confirmed on an AHFC page). Comes with a 30-year fixed AHFC loan; ask an AHFC-approved lender.
programs.source: First National Bank Alaska lender page (AHFC-run program, 3% or 4% of loan by credit); no current AHFC program page found

programs.name: HOME Opportunity Program (HOP)
programs.amountText: Down payment/closing-cost help for low-income buyers — amount set by the provider (not published)
programs.notes: AHFC's HOP page lists Alaska Community Development Corp. as provider (Fairbanks, Mat-Su, Kenai, Juneau, Ketchikan, Sitka, Kodiak and other areas — not Anchorage). Buyer terms (grant vs. lien) aren't published, so shown conservatively as deferred. AHFC says no grant funding is available for new allocating agencies; funds subject to availability.

Anchorage.name: Home$tart Grant (Cook Inlet Lending Center)
Anchorage.agency: Cook Inlet Lending Center (AHFC-listed Anchorage-area DPA provider)
Anchorage.notes: Called a grant, with a 5-year owner-occupancy requirement; repayment/recapture terms aren't spelled out, so shown conservatively as deferred. Homebuyer education required; one grant per household; requires a first-mortgage application in process with CILC. CILC says it is discontinuing brokered mortgage lending — confirm availability (907-793-3058).

Anchorage.name: NAHI Grant (Cook Inlet Lending Center)
Anchorage.notes: For Alaska Native, American Indian or Native Hawaiian buyers (tribal card or corporation letter required). Called a grant with a 5-year owner-occupancy requirement; recapture terms not published, so shown as deferred. Homebuyer education; first-mortgage application with CILC required. Confirm availability given CILC's wind-down of brokered lending.

Anchorage.name: Down Payment Assistance Loan (Cook Inlet Lending Center)
Anchorage.notes: Fully repayable fixed-rate 30-year second mortgage (CILC's example uses 5%; actual rate varies). Special Purpose Credit Program: Alaska Native/American Indian/Native Hawaiian borrowers anywhere in Alaska; others only in CDFI Fund-designated Native Communities. No bankruptcy/foreclosure in 6 years; 2 months' reserves; HUD-approved education; pre-approval before signing a contract.

programs.name: Step Up DPA
programs.notes: 10-year second mortgage paired with a 30-year fixed first mortgage from AHFA.

programs.name: Affordable Income Subsidy Grant
programs.notes: Closing costs only; HFA Advantage conventional loan only.

Huntsville.name: Down Payment Assistance
Huntsville.notes: 0% second, no payments; forgiven after 5 years in the home.

Mobile.name: Down Payment Assistance
Mobile.notes: Older source — confirm the program is still funded.

programs.name: Arkansas Dream Down Payment Initiative
programs.amountText: Up to $25,000 per ADFA's FY2023 report (earlier data said 10% of price / $10,000) — confirm with ADFA
programs.notes: 5-year forgivable second mortgage for lower-income buyers (by area median income), per ADFA's FY2023 report. ADFA's current home-loan pages no longer list it — confirm availability with ADFA (501-682-5466).
programs.source: ADFA FY2023 Annual Report of Program Activity (adfa.arkansas.gov, >1 year old); not listed on ADFA's current homeloans pages

programs.name: ADFA Down Payment Assistance
programs.notes: Second mortgage with a 10-year term; requires an ADFA StartSmart or Move-Up first mortgage.

Little Rock.name: City of Little Rock Down Payment Assistance
Little Rock.agency: City of Little Rock Community Development
Little Rock.notes: Forgiven in equal monthly installments over 60 months. Home must be in Little Rock city limits and owner-occupied for 5 years; no ownership in past 3 years; city-approved counseling; first mortgage from a lender with an Arkansas office, which requests the assistance; repairs completed before approval.

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.agency: Arizona IDA / Arizona Dept. of Housing

programs.name: HOME+PLUS DPA
programs.amountText: Up to 4% (applied to first-mortgage amount per Arizona IDA FAQ example)
programs.notes: 0% deferred soft second, no payments, fully forgiven after 60 months; repaid if sold or refinanced within 5 years. Non-forgivable options also offered. Not limited to first-time buyers. Available year-round statewide; self-funded with no sunset. Homebuyer education required.

programs.name: Arizona Is Home
programs.incomeNote: ≤100% AMI by county (e.g., Pinal $112,400, Yavapai $92,200; eff. 7/1/2026)
programs.notes: PAUSED: Arizona IDA says 2026 funds are exhausted and the program is retired for the rest of 2026 (as of 10/6/2026); annual funding resumes next year. Non-forgivable 0% deferred second, due on sale or refinance, paired with a below-market 30-year fixed first mortgage. First-time buyers (exceptions for qualified veterans and targeted areas). Not offered in Maricopa or Pima Counties or Chino Valley.

Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).name: Home in Five Advantage
Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).amountText: 3%, 4%, 5% or 6% of loan (FHA/VA); 0–6% conventional, depending on option
Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).notes: Phoenix & Maricopa County IDAs. 0% forgivable second: 3-year (forgiven monthly over 36 months), 7-year 'Arizona is Home' option (first-time, ≤120% AMI, 6-month AZ residency) or 30-year; a 10-year 6% amortizing option also exists. No USDA. Earlier '6% for educators/first responders' claim not found in program documents — removed. Homepage (Nov 2026) confirms up to 6%, 640 FICO, income ≤ $153,440; azishome page confirms 7-year option (first-time, 6-month AZ residency, income ≤ $131,520). Full term options rest on the Aug 2025 program description (>1 yr old).
Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).source: Home in Five Advantage official program description (Aug 2025) + homein5advantage.com/azishome

Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).name: Home in Five Platinum
Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).amountText: 4% (FHA/VA); basis not stated on administrator page
Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).notes: Mortgage revenue bond program (2025B bond). PAUSED: administrator (eHousingPlus) page shows the bond as 'Fully originated' — no funds available until a new bond issue. First-time (no ownership in 3 years); conventional/USDA only ≤80% AMI. Forgiveness term not stated.

Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).name: Open Doors DPA
Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).amountText: Up to 10% of purchase price, based on need
Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).notes: 0% deferred loan, fully forgiven after the affordability period (up to 15 years depending on amount); repaid if sold, refinanced or no longer owner-occupied during that period. Must meet the FHA first-time homebuyer definition. City of Phoenix only; price ≤ 95% of $470,250 HUD median (~$446,738); fixed-rate, fully amortizing first mortgage ≤30 years; 8-hour education + HUD counseling. Fact sheet (Aug 25, 2026) notes funding reservations are limited.

Tucson / Pima County.name: Tucson-Pima County HOME Consortium DPA
Tucson / Pima County.amountText: Lesser of $50,000 or 20% of price, based on need
Tucson / Pima County.notes: Deferred, no monthly payments; 2% interest accrues during the affordability period (5 yrs ≤$15k, 10 yrs $15k–$40k, 15 yrs >$40k) and is forgiven, but principal is repaid at sale. $1,000 own funds + 2 months reserves; home warranty required. Price ≤ $304,000 existing / $345,000 new. Apply via partner agencies (ARC, Chicanos Por La Causa, Pima County CLT); counseling before contract. FHA, VA or conventional QM; no ARMs. Per June 2026 fact sheet.
Tucson / Pima County.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI (4-person $79,850, 2025 HUD limits per June 2026 fact sheet)

Tucson / Pima County.name: Pima Tucson Homebuyer Solution
Tucson / Pima County.amountText: Up to 100% of cash needed to close; % not published
Tucson / Pima County.notes: Pima County IDA. 3-year forgivable second (PTHS); 'PTHS Advantage' option is 30-year forgivable. Grant for VA loans. No first-time or price limit; income limits apply; 45% max DTI. Combinable with City/County HOME DPA.

Tucson / Pima County.name: Arizona Is Home (Pima IDA)
Tucson / Pima County.notes: PAUSED: Pima IDA page marked 'Currently unavailable'. 30-year forgivable second with a 30-year fixed assisted-rate first mortgage; first-time buyers with 6 months AZ residency; all of Pima County incl. Tucson. Credit requirement not stated.

programs.name: MyHome Assistance
programs.amountText: Up to 3.5% of price/appraised value with CalHFA FHA; up to 3% with CalHFA Conventional, VA or USDA
programs.notes: Deferred-payment junior loan; must be paired with a CalHFA first mortgage. 640 min credit per CalHFA government-loan matrix (01/2026; 700 for DTI up to 50%); conventional pairing may require a higher score. Rate varies and is not published.

programs.name: Zero Interest Program (ZIP)
programs.amountText: 2% or 3% of first loan amount, closing costs and prepaids only
programs.notes: Used only with CalPLUS FHA first mortgage, in third-lien position behind MyHome. Repayment terms not stated on matrix; treated conservatively as deferred.

programs.name: Dream For All Shared Appreciation Loan
programs.amountText: Lesser of 20% of price/appraised value or $150,000
programs.incomeNote: Dream For All county income limits (e.g. ~$168k LA County, ~$309k Santa Clara County in 2026)
programs.notes: First-generation homebuyer required. Repay principal plus 20% of appreciation (15% if income at/below 80% AMI) on sale, transfer or payoff of first. Must use Dream For All Conventional first. 2026 application window closed March 16, 2026; vouchers issued by random selection; no future round dates announced.

City of Los Angeles.name: Low Income Purchase Assistance (LIPA)
City of Los Angeles.amountText: Up to $161,000 for down payment, closing costs and acquisition
City of Los Angeles.incomeNote: Low-income (~80% AMI; 2025 limit $121,150 for household of 4)
City of Los Angeles.notes: 0% deferred loan plus shared appreciation, due on sale/transfer/payoff or at 30 years. Funds reserved in limited rounds (last listed round March 4, 2026); call LAHD for current availability. First-time = no ownership in past 3 years. Eligible first-mortgage types not specified by LAHD.

City of Los Angeles.name: Moderate Income Purchase Assistance (MIPA)
City of Los Angeles.amountText: Up to $115,000 for down payment, closing costs and acquisition
City of Los Angeles.notes: 0% deferred loan plus shared appreciation, due on sale/transfer/payoff or 30-year balloon. Reserved in rounds (next listed Dec 16, 2026). Eligible first-mortgage types not specified by LAHD.

Los Angeles County.name: Home Ownership Program (HOP80 / HOP150)
Los Angeles County.amountText: Lesser of $100,000 or 20% of purchase price
Los Angeles County.incomeNote: HOP80 up to 80% AMI (price cap $700k); HOP150 up to 150% AMI (price cap $850k)
Los Angeles County.notes: 0% deferred shared-equity loan repaid with share of appreciation on sale/transfer/non-occupancy. Unincorporated LA County and participating cities only (not City of LA). First-come, first-served via participating lenders. Min credit and first-mortgage types not stated by LACDA.

City of San Diego.name: First-Time Homebuyer Program (Low-Income)
City of San Diego.amountText: Deferred loan up to 17% of price (max $125,000) plus forgivable closing-cost grant of 4% up to $10,000
City of San Diego.incomeNote: At or below 80% AMI; max price $883,025
City of San Diego.notes: 3% simple interest, payments deferred 30 years unless sold/no longer occupied. Requires fixed-rate first and 3% buyer down payment. SDHC intro text says up to 19% but program table says 17% (used here). Previous 22% figure applies to the County of San Diego program, not the City. No published min score ('good credit').

City of San Diego.name: First-Time Homebuyer Program (Middle-Income)
City of San Diego.notes: Loan at 4% simple interest deferred years 1-5, then amortizes over 120 months; the $10,000 grant is forgiven after 3 years of owner occupancy. ZIP codes beginning 921 only.

San Francisco.name: Downpayment Assistance Loan Program (DALP)
San Francisco.agency: SF Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development (MOHCD)
San Francisco.incomeNote: Up to ~200% AMI ($311,700 for household of 4)
San Francisco.notes: Silent second; repay principal plus share of appreciation on sale. Lottery-based: 2025 application period closed June 2, 2025; no 2026 round announced on sf.gov.

Santa Clara County / San Jose.name: Homebuyer Empowerment Loan Program (HELP)
Santa Clara County / San Jose.notes: Agency lists 'All Funds Allocated'. Repayment terms not published on page; treated conservatively as deferred. Replaces Empower Homebuyers SCC, which closed and sunset June 30, 2026.

programs.name: CHFA DPA Grant
programs.amountText: Lesser of 3% of first mortgage or $25,000
programs.notes: No repayment. Requires a CHFA first mortgage. First-generation buyers and borrowers with a permanent disability may get up to $25,000 regardless of loan size.

programs.name: CHFA Second Mortgage Loan
programs.amountText: Lesser of 4% of first mortgage or $25,000
programs.notes: Repayment deferred until payoff, sale, refinance, or the home is no longer your primary residence. First mortgage carries a higher rate than with the grant.

Colorado Springs / El Paso County.name: Turnkey Plus
Colorado Springs / El Paso County.notes: Half forgiven over 5 years; half deferred until payoff.

programs.name: Time To Own
programs.notes: 0% loan, no monthly payments, 10% forgiven each year. Requires a CHFA first mortgage and 3 years of Connecticut residency. Repeat buyers qualify in targeted areas.

Bridgeport.name: Down Payment Program
Bridgeport.notes: Forgiven over 5, 10 or 15 years depending on amount.

New Haven.name: Down Payment & Closing Cost Assistance
New Haven.notes: Fixed cash assistance added to an NH Housing mortgage, for down payment and closing costs. Forgiveness terms: confirm with NH Housing.

programs.name: DC Open Doors DPAL
programs.amountText: Covers the minimum required down payment
programs.notes: 0% loan, no monthly payments; due after 30 years or at sale, refinance or move-out. First-time and repeat buyers.

programs.name: Home Purchase Assistance Program (HPAP)
programs.amountText: Up to $202,000 gap financing + $4,000 closing costs
programs.notes: Under 80% AMI: deferred until sale, cash-out refinance or move-out. 80–110% MFI: payments deferred 5 years, then repaid over 40 years.

programs.name: Employer-Assisted Housing (DC employees)
programs.notes: DC government employees; first responders/educators get a different tier.

programs.name: DC4ME VA loan assistance
programs.notes: For qualified military-connected borrowers with a VA loan. Structure of the 3% not published — confirm with DCHFA.

programs.name: First State
programs.notes: 0% second mortgage, no monthly payment; due at refinance, sale, title transfer or move-out. Through DSHA Welcome Home (first-time) or Open Door (repeat buyers).

programs.name: Keys4You
programs.notes: 0% deferred second; Welcome Home (first-time) or Open Door (repeat buyers).

programs.name: Take5
programs.notes: 0% deferred second; Welcome Home (first-time buyers) only.

programs.name: Diamond in the Rough
programs.notes: 0% deferred second for homes needing minor repairs; requires the FHA 203(k) Limited program. Welcome Home (first-time buyers) only. Due at refinance, sale, title transfer or move-out.

Wilmington / New Castle County.name: First Start Homebuyer Program (City of Wilmington)
Wilmington / New Castle County.agency: City of Wilmington Dept. of Real Estate and Housing
Wilmington / New Castle County.amountText: Up to $15,000 (lesser of $15,000 or 6% of price) for down payment/closing costs; up to $25,000 more for affordability based on income and debt
Wilmington / New Castle County.incomeNote: ≤ 80% AMI for CDBG funds (city funds have allowed up to 100% AMI)
Wilmington / New Castle County.notes: City of Wilmington homes. Buyer contributes at least $1,000; fixed-rate mortgage ≤30 years with no points/origination fees. Repayment/forgiveness terms aren't published, so shown conservatively as deferred. City added $350,000 in its FY2024/25 plan amendment; no application window posted — call 311 / (302) 576-2620.

Wilmington / New Castle County.name: Down Payment & Settlement Assistance (DPS)
Wilmington / New Castle County.agency: New Castle County Dept. of Community Services
Wilmington / New Castle County.notes: Repayable 15-year loan for down payment/settlement costs: no payments for the first 2 years, monthly payments from year 3. Rate, income limits and whether City of Wilmington addresses qualify aren't on the page — contact the county (302-395-5698).

programs.name: Florida Assist (FL Assist)
programs.notes: Due in full on sale, transfer, refinance, satisfaction of first mortgage or non-occupancy. Requires a Florida Housing first mortgage; IRS first-time buyer definition (no ownership in 3 years).

programs.name: Florida Homeownership Loan Program (FL HLP) Second Mortgage
programs.amountText: $12,500 at 3%, fully amortizing over 30 years (monthly payment)
programs.notes: Payment counts in DTI; balance due on sale/refinance. Requires a Florida Housing first mortgage (agency page does not itemize loan types for HLP).

programs.name: 3%, 4% and 5% HFA Preferred / HFA Advantage PLUS Second Mortgage
programs.amountText: 3%, 4% or 5% of total first mortgage loan amount
programs.notes: Forgiven 20% per year over 5 years. Only with conventional HFA Preferred / HFA Advantage (TBA) first mortgages. pct shown is the minimum tier (3%).

programs.name: Florida Hometown Heroes Housing Program
programs.amountText: 5% of first mortgage loan amount, min $10,000, max $35,000; 0%, 30-year deferred, not forgivable
programs.notes: Full-time employees of Florida-based employers in health care, schools, first responders/public safety, courts, child care; active military/reserves/Guard; veterans. 2025-26 funds were fully committed Feb 2026; agency page now shows the HTH 2026 program (limits dated 7-13-26) and no exhaustion notice as of 2026-11-20. Funded in rounds, may close without notice. minCredit is Florida Housing's first-mortgage minimum.

Jacksonville.name: Head Start to Homeownership (H2H)
Jacksonville.agency: City of Jacksonville Housing & Community Development
Jacksonville.amountText: Up to $25,000 for down payment and closing costs
Jacksonville.incomeNote: At or below 80% of Duval County AMI
Jacksonville.notes: City page does not publish rate, term or forgiveness (contact program) - shown conservatively as deferred. Subject to funding limitations; home must pass HQS inspection. Loan types not specified.

Tampa.name: Dare to Own the Dream (DARE)
Tampa.agency: City of Tampa Housing & Community Development
Tampa.incomeNote: 50.01%-140% AMI; households under 50% AMI not eligible
Tampa.notes: 0% deferred silent second, forgiven after 20 years of occupancy. Purchase price cap $450,000; max back-end DTI 50%; buyer invests $2,000 ($1,000 own funds). City of Tampa limits only. City release 2026-10-28 says applications open.

Hillsborough County.name: Home Sweet Home Hillsborough
Hillsborough County.agency: Housing Finance Authority of Hillsborough County
Hillsborough County.amountText: Amount not published by HFA/administrator; 0% deferred 30-year second, never forgiven
Hillsborough County.notes: Countywide incl. Tampa. Repaid on sale/refinance/non-occupancy. First-time rule waived in Targeted Areas. Max price $450,000. Includes MCC. Page published by program administrator eHousingPlus, linked from hillsboroughcountyhfa.org.

Miami-Dade County.name: Homebuyer Down Payment Assistance Program
Miami-Dade County.amountText: Up to $35,000; 0% deferred, up to 30 years
Miami-Dade County.notes: Principal due on sale, transfer, refinance or death; County shares resale profit if sold within 6 years (100% yrs 1-3, 50% yrs 4-6). Fixed-rate first mortgage, CLTV max 105%, buyer contributes 1%. County residency required. Funding status not posted.

North Miami.name: First-Time Homebuyer Assistance (SHIP/HOME)
North Miami.notes: City calls it a forgivable deferred loan but does not publish the forgiveness schedule (affordability period 7 yrs SHIP / up to 15 yrs HOME) - shown conservatively as deferred. Open until funds are depleted. Max price $460,000 SHIP / $370,000 HOME.

Broward County.name: Homebuyer Purchase Assistance (HPA)
Broward County.amountText: Varies by participating city (county flyer cites up to $50,000-$120,000 in some communities); 0% deferred, 15-year term
Broward County.notes: Funds by city; June 2026 county flyer shows NO FUNDS for many communities - first-come, first-qualified. Buyer contributes 3% (not VA). Max price ~$679,324. Forgiveness not stated - shown as deferred.

Orlando.name: Orange County Homebuyer Down Payment Assistance
Orlando.notes: Closed to new applications (waitlist); anticipated reopening March 1, 2027, subject to state funding. Loan terms not published - shown conservatively as deferred.

Orlando.name: City of Orlando Down Payment Assistance
Orlando.agency: City of Orlando Housing & Community Development
Orlando.notes: Forgiven after 10 years if owner-occupied. Fixed-rate first mortgage from City-registered lender. City is not accepting new applications.

programs.name: Georgia Dream — Standard
programs.incomeNote: Income and price limits by county
programs.notes: 0% second mortgage, no monthly payment; repaid at sale or refinance. Homebuyer education required. Must use a Georgia Dream first mortgage.

programs.name: Georgia Dream — PEN / CHOICE
programs.incomeNote: Income and price limits by county
programs.notes: For protectors, educators, health-care workers and active military (PEN), or households with a member with a disability (CHOICE). 0% deferred second.

programs.name: Georgia Dream — Peach Plus
programs.amountText: Amount set by DCA — confirm with lender
programs.incomeNote: Higher limits: income to ~$237K, price to ~$725K
programs.notes: Open to repeat buyers. 0% deferred second.

City of Atlanta.name: ATL HomeNOW
City of Atlanta.notes: Down payment, closing costs and/or permanent rate reduction. Forgiven after 10 years as primary residence (Invest Atlanta page). Invest Atlanta also offers ATL Home Renovation Advantage ($10K), Perry Bolton and Vine City programs (area-specific).

City of Atlanta.name: Beltline Mortgage Assistance Program
City of Atlanta.amountText: Up to $20,000; up to $30,000 for legacy residents & public servants
City of Atlanta.incomeNote: 120% AMI (140% AMI tier available); Beltline TAD subareas 1, 2, 3, 8, 9, 10 only
City of Atlanta.notes: 0% soft second mortgage with 15-year affordability period; forgiveness terms not stated, so shown as deferred to be conservative. Up to $30,000 for civil servants and legacy residents. Max loan $400,000. 8-hour homebuyer education required.

City of Atlanta.name: Atlanta Housing Down Payment Assistance
City of Atlanta.amountText: Up to $20,000; up to $25,000 for public safety, healthcare, education, military/veterans and Housing Choice Voucher participants
City of Atlanta.notes: 0% community second; forgiven after 10 years of owner-occupancy with declining recapture (100% yrs 1-5, then 80/60/40/20%). First-time = no ownership in past 3 years. Fixed-rate conventional, FHA or VA first mortgage. Earlier $60K voucher-holder figure not found on Atlanta Housing site.

Fulton County (outside City of Atlanta).name: Fulton County Homeownership Program (HOP)
Fulton County (outside City of Atlanta).amountText: Up to $22,500 based on need (no % cap stated in 2026 guidelines)
Fulton County (outside City of Atlanta).incomeNote: At or below 80% AMI (4-person $94,250, eff. June 1, 2026); max price $347,000 existing / $367,000-$371,000 new
Fulton County (outside City of Atlanta).notes: 0% deferred second, no monthly payment; forgiven 20% per year over 5-year affordability period (HOP guidelines rev. June 2026). Down payment, closing costs and/or rate buydown. Guidelines list conventional/FHA/VA (USDA mentioned inconsistently). No set minimum credit score. HOME-funded, first come first ready until funds run out.

Gwinnett County.name: Homestretch Down Payment Assistance
Gwinnett County.notes: 0% no-payment soft second, forgiven 20% per year over 5-year affordability period. Fixed-rate FHA, VA or conventional only (no 203k). Single-family, townhome or condo. First-time = no ownership in 3 years.

DeKalb County.name: DeKalb HomeStart
DeKalb County.amountText: Amount not yet published by DeKalb County (news reports cited ~$20,000)
DeKalb County.notes: Announced July 14, 2026 as part of the $155M housing investment bond: down payment, closing cost and rate buydown help, enhanced for first responders/public servants. No application or terms published on county site yet; type shown as deferred to be conservative.

DeKalb County.name: WE DeKalb
DeKalb County.amountText: 1%-3% grant of loan amount (program not currently available)
DeKalb County.notes: eHousingPlus program page (Aug 2026): 'as previously offered, is not currently available' and under strategic review. Non-repayable grant when offered.

Savannah.name: DreamMaker Home Purchase Assistance
Savannah.amountText: Up to $30,000 (up to $50,000 for city-partnered homes)
Savannah.incomeNote: Income limits apply; city limits only
Savannah.notes: 2% interest, 30-year deferred-payment loan (city page); up to $50,000 for city-partnered housing. Forgiveness not stated. Year-round while funds remain. Credit and loan-type rules not stated on city page.

Augusta-Richmond County.name: Homeownership Assistance Program
Augusta-Richmond County.amountText: Up to $10,000 toward down payment and closing costs
Augusta-Richmond County.notes: Augusta HCD lists up to $10,000 (previously shown as $5,000); repayment/forgiveness terms not stated, so shown as deferred to be conservative. Subject to available funding; rolling review. City/RCSO employees may get up to $15,000 (Officer Next Door).

Columbus.name: Sweet Home Columbus
Columbus.incomeNote: At or below 80% AMI (4-person $67,750); max price ~$252,000 (HOME limit)
Columbus.notes: 0% deferred loan (city page); 2026 policy (eff. July 1, 2026) describes pro-rated forgiveness over 5 yrs (<$25K) or 10 yrs ($25K+), while the web page says residency up to 15 years, so shown as deferred to be conservative. Fixed-rate 30-year first mortgage only. 8-hour counseling required. First-time = no ownership in 3 years.

Cobb County.name: Cobb County My Home DPA
Cobb County.agency: Housing Authority of Cobb County (administered by eHousingPlus)
Cobb County.amountText: 1% or 2% of loan amount grant (+$10,000 for Cobb County employees; $10K-$15K for eligible City of Marietta employees)
Cobb County.incomeNote: Income limits apply (approx. $90,800 at 80% AMI / $159,880 higher tier per Aug 2025 guide)
Cobb County.notes: Non-repayable grant paired with program 30-year fixed first mortgage; no second lien. No first-time buyer requirement. Min FICO 640 (VA/Freddie HFA Advantage), 660 FHA. Terms from program guide rev. 08-27-25.

Clayton County.name: Clayton County Down Payment Assistance Program
Clayton County.agency: Clayton County Office of Grants Administration (HUD)
Clayton County.amountText: Up to $7,500; up to $10,000 for veterans/spouses, county employees, law enforcement, first responders, healthcare and education workers
Clayton County.incomeNote: At or below 80% AMI; max purchase price $270,000
Clayton County.notes: Interest-free soft second, fully forgiven after 5 or 10 years of occupancy depending on amount. Lender sets credit minimum. No condos or mobile homes; $1,000 buyer contribution; 8-hour HUD education. Eligible first-mortgage types not listed (all shown). First-time = no ownership in 3 years.

programs.name: Deferred Closing Cost Assistance Loan
programs.amountText: Up to $10,000 (Honolulu County: up to $5,000); requires $5,000 borrower match
programs.notes: 0% loan for closing costs incl. rate buydowns; deferred 15 years or until sale, title change, non-occupancy or equity take-out; annual occupancy affidavit. HHOC Mortgage must originate the first mortgage; homebuyer education + coaching required; no ownership in past 3 years. Funds limited, reserved at contract. Eligible first-mortgage types not stated.

programs.name: Down Payment Assistance Loan (DPAL)
programs.amountText: Second loan up to $125,000 at 4.5% or the first-mortgage rate, whichever is lower
programs.notes: 30-year amortizing second; 3% minimum down payment; no mortgage insurance or prepayment penalty. HHOC Mortgage must originate the first mortgage; homebuyer education + coaching required. Eligible first-mortgage types not stated.

programs.name: Max HLPR (Home Loan Payment Relief) Loan
programs.amountText: Amount not published — contact HHOC Mortgage
programs.notes: 0% deferred down payment loan with a shared-appreciation equity agreement; principal due after 20 years or earlier on sale, non-occupancy or cash-out refinance/HELOC. HHOC Mortgage must originate the first mortgage.

programs.name: Mortgage Booster (pilot)
programs.amountText: Up to $50,000 second loan at fixed 3%
programs.notes: Pilot program; 30-year amortizing second that boosts qualifying amount; 3% minimum down payment. HHOC Mortgage must originate the first mortgage.

programs.name: Hale Kamaʻāina Mortgage Program – Down Payment Second
programs.agency: Hawaii Housing Finance and Development Corporation (HHFDC)
programs.amountText: Soft second mortgage equal to 4% of the first-mortgage amount
programs.incomeNote: County/targeted-area limits (e.g., Honolulu non-targeted 2025: $152,000 for 1–2 persons, $174,800 for 3+)
programs.notes: Optional soft second (1% simple interest, no monthly payments, due at maturity/sale/refi/transfer) with HHFDC's below-market Hale Kamaʻāina first mortgage; borrower must contribute 5% of price. Second-mortgage terms are being updated under Act 214 (2026) pending rule amendments; confirm with a participating lender.

Honolulu (City & County of Honolulu).name: Down Payment Loan Program
Honolulu (City & County of Honolulu).agency: City & County of Honolulu Department of Community Services
Honolulu (City & County of Honolulu).amountText: Up to $40,000 at 0% interest, repaid over 20 years (about $167/month at the max)
Honolulu (City & County of Honolulu).notes: HOME-funded 0% amortizing second for buyers who own no primary residence; first-come, first-served subject to funds. City-approved homebuyer education and City inspection required; lender submits the loan packet.

programs.name: Military Homeownership Assistance
programs.notes: Funds remain for fiscal 2027 (about $1.1 million as of Nov 2, 2026). For eligible service members and veterans.

Davenport.name: First-Time Home Buyer Grant
Davenport.amountText: Half your down payment + closing costs, up to $10,000

programs.name: Idaho Housing Second Mortgage
programs.amountText: Up to 8% of the sales price (lesser of price or appraised value)
programs.notes: Second mortgage at a fixed rate 2 points above your first mortgage, repaid in monthly payments over 15 years. Available to all eligible Idaho buyers, not only first-time buyers. You contribute at least $500 of your own funds. Finally Home!® education required.

programs.name: Idaho Housing Forgivable Loan
programs.notes: Raises the first-mortgage rate slightly. Idaho Housing's DPA page mentions a forgivable-loan option but publishes no amount or forgiveness terms; figures here are from a secondary guide—confirm with an Idaho Housing lender.
programs.source: The Mortgage Reports state guide (Nov 2026); Idaho Housing DPA page mentions a forgivable option without terms

Boise.name: Homeownership Opportunity Program (HOP)
Boise.agency: City of Boise Housing & Community Development
Boise.amountText: Up to $45,000 ($65,000 for Community Land Trust / deed-restricted homes)
Boise.incomeNote: Household income 50%–80% AMI; home within Boise city limits
Boise.notes: Deferred mortgage for down payment, closing costs and/or direct assistance; due at sale or transfer. Shared appreciation: repayment = assistance × (future sale price ÷ purchase price), capped at net proceeds. Apply only by referral through NeighborWorks Boise or LEAP Housing. First mortgage must be 30-year fixed. Loan types not specified (shown as all).
Boise.source: City of Boise HOP Policy (2025 revision); program page confirms program, income range and referral process

programs.name: IHDA Access Forgivable
programs.incomeNote: IHDA income and purchase price limits apply (see ihdamortgage.org/limits)
programs.notes: Forgiven monthly over 10 years. Paired with IHDA 30-yr fixed first mortgage; conventional = Fannie HFA Preferred / Freddie HFA Advantage. Buyer contribution greater of $1,000 or 1%; max DTI 50%; homebuyer counseling required. IHDA notes funding can change at any time.

programs.name: IHDA Access Deferred
programs.incomeNote: IHDA income and purchase price limits apply (see ihdamortgage.org/limits)
programs.notes: Interest-free, deferred for the life of the first mortgage; repaid on sale, refinance or payoff. Buyer contribution greater of $1,000 or 1%; max DTI 50%; counseling required.

programs.name: IHDA Access Repayable
programs.incomeNote: IHDA income and purchase price limits apply (see ihdamortgage.org/limits)
programs.notes: Zero-interest second loan repaid in monthly installments over 10 years. Buyer contribution greater of $1,000 or 1%; max DTI 50%; counseling required.

programs.name: IHDA Access Home
programs.incomeNote: IHDA income and purchase price limits apply (see ihdamortgage.org/limits)
programs.notes: Interest-free, deferred for life of the mortgage; repaid on sale, refinance or payoff. First-time buyers only, except eligible veterans (COE/DD214) or purchases in IHDA targeted areas. Buyer contribution greater of $1,000 or 1%; max DTI 50%.

programs.name: IHDA Opening Doors
programs.incomeNote: IHDA income and purchase price limits apply (see ihdamortgage.org/limits)
programs.notes: Forgiven monthly over 5 years; unforgiven balance repaid if sold/refinanced earlier. First-time and repeat buyers. Listed as 'Now Open' on ihdamortgage.org.

Aurora.name: Choose Aurora Homebuyer Assistance
Aurora.amountText: $20,000 0% deferred loan, plus $5,000 closing-cost grant for households ≤80% AMI (up to $2,000 small-repairs grant may also apply)
Aurora.incomeNote: ≤120% AMI (e.g. $145,800 for household of 4); $5,000 grant only ≤80% AMI
Aurora.notes: Deferred soft second repaid on sale, title change, cash-out refi or end of owner occupancy; no forgiveness stated. Max $25,000 assumes ≤80% AMI ($20,000 for 81–120% AMI); city page cites up to $27,000 incl. repair grant. Amount set by city staff based on need. First-time rule, credit score and loan types not stated by city. Funding availability not stated; HUD counseling required.

Joliet.name: Joliet Down Payment Assistance Program
Joliet.amountText: Minimum $1,000; maximum up to 20% of purchase price (no dollar cap published)
Joliet.notes: City page states the program is not currently taking applications. 0% deferred loan described as forgivable, but forgiveness period is not published, so typed conservatively as deferred. Buyer must contribute $2,500. Replaces prior 'Illinois Assist' listing, which is not a City of Joliet program.

Chicago.name: HomeGrown Purchase Assistance Grant
Chicago.agency: City of Chicago Dept. of Housing (administered by NLS and TRP Lending)
Chicago.amountText: Up to $70,000 (Zone A) or $50,000 (Zone B), capped at 25% of purchase price
Chicago.incomeNote: Zone A ≤120% AMI; Zone B ≤150% AMI
Chicago.notes: Forgiven 1/60 per month over 5 years of owner occupancy. Buyer cannot own any other home at purchase. Fixed-rate first mortgage required; max back-end DTI 38%; no 3–4 unit buildings. First-come, first-served; waitlist possible if funds run out. Terms confirmed on administrator NHS Chicago/NLS page (updated Jul 2026); chicago.gov page could not be fetched. Min credit not published.

Cook County.name: Cook County Down Payment Assistance Program
Cook County.agency: Cook County Bureau of Economic Development
Cook County.amountText: 5% of first loan amount, up to $25,000
Cook County.incomeNote: ≤120% AMI ($145,800 for household of 4); no income limit in Disproportionately Impacted Areas / Qualified Census Tracts
Cook County.notes: Phase III ($2M, ~100 buyers) launched Jul 20, 2026 through participating lenders; funds limited and may run out. Forgivable second over 5 years; usable for down payment, closing costs or rate buydown. First-time and repeat buyers per county page (first-timers need HUD counseling). Formerly listed here as 'Home Advantage'.

Kane County.name: Kane County First-Time Homebuyer Loan Program
Kane County.agency: Kane County Office of Community Reinvestment
Kane County.amountText: Up to $10,000 (additional $10,000 possible in St. Charles)
Kane County.incomeNote: Federal HOME income limits (figures not published on page)
Kane County.notes: 0% deferred loan repaid on sale, transfer or end of principal residence. Excludes City of Aurora (see Aurora) and Hampshire, Huntley, Hoffman Estates, Montgomery; includes Elgin. Must live/work in area 1 yr, 1% down, HUD counseling. Funding availability not stated.

Rockford.name: Rockford Homebuyer Assistance Program
Rockford.notes: City page states the program is closed for applications. 5-year forgivable loan (occupancy described as ~6 years); unoccupied detached single-family homes within city limits only.

programs.name: First Step
programs.amountText: Up to 4% of price (Oct 2026 program guide; earlier 2026 materials said 5%)
programs.incomeNote: County income and purchase price limits apply
programs.notes: Bond-funded replacement for First Place. Non-forgivable second, due when the first mortgage ends or the home is no longer your primary residence; federal recapture tax may apply. First-time rule waived in targeted census tracts and for qualified veterans. 30-year fixed FHA or Fannie/Freddie conventional. Min credit 660 (680 if DTI 45-50%).

programs.name: Next Home
programs.amountText: 2.5% or 3.5% of price (lesser of price or appraised value)
programs.notes: Non-forgivable 0% second; due in full when the first mortgage ends (sale, refinance, payoff) or the home stops being your primary residence. First-time and repeat buyers; income limits only. 30-year fixed FHA or Fannie/Freddie conventional. Min credit 660 (680 if DTI 45-50%) per IHCDA lender matrix 05/2026.

Indianapolis.name: Down Payment & Closing Cost Assistance
Indianapolis.incomeNote: Income limits (HUD Marion County); Marion County only, not Lawrence, Beech Grove, Southport or Speedway
Indianapolis.notes: Only available with an INHP in-house mortgage (no mortgage insurance, 1-3% down). Repayment/forgiveness terms not published, so treated as deferred. Subject to funding.

Evansville.name: Homebuyer Program
Evansville.notes: HOME-funded 0% loan, forgiven over the affordability period: 5 years under $15,000, 10 years for $15,000-$40,000, 15 years over $40,000. Repayable from net proceeds if sold or vacated early. Amount is based on need; the $40,000 figure is from a third-party guide.
Evansville.source: City of Evansville homebuyer program guidelines (2018) + The Mortgage Reports state guide (Nov 2026)
Evansville.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI; Evansville city limits; price ≤95% of area median

Fort Wayne.name: Hoosier Homes
Fort Wayne.amountText: Up to 5% for down payment and closing costs
Fort Wayne.incomeNote: Up to 140% AMI by county (Allen County $133,569 in 2026); county price limits
Fort Wayne.notes: 0% second with no payments, 7-year term, paired with a 30-year fixed first mortgage from a participating lender. First-time and repeat buyers (first-timers need 8-hour education). Available in 26 Indiana counties including Allen, Marion and Lake. FWHA lists 640 min credit (administrator site says 620). Whether 5% is of price or loan and which loan types qualify are not stated; shown conservatively.

programs.name: First-Time Homebuyer Program
programs.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI; not in Topeka, Lawrence, Wichita, KCK or Johnson County

Wichita.name: HOMEownership 80
Wichita.amountText: Up to 20% of price + $2,000 closing costs
Wichita.notes: Half forgiven after 5 or 10 years depending on amount.

Louisville Metro.name: Down Payment Assistance
Louisville Metro.notes: 0% loan; half forgivable over time, rest due at sale or refinance.

programs.name: MRB Home grant
programs.notes: Below-market rate. LHC is moving programs to its HomeStart lineup — confirm this one is still offered.

programs.name: HomeStart Advantage (Keys for Service)
programs.notes: For full-time law enforcement, firefighters, paramedics and certified teachers. Forgivable assistance.

programs.name: HomeStart Assist
programs.notes: 0% forgivable second mortgage with a 30-year fixed first mortgage at about market rate. First-time and repeat buyers.

programs.name: HomeStart Plus (disaster-affected areas)
programs.notes: Enhanced assistance for homes in designated disaster-affected parishes. Amount from earlier Resilience Soft Second terms — confirm with LHC.

programs.name: MassHousing DPA Option 1
programs.notes: 0% interest, deferred until sale, refinance or first-mortgage payoff. Income-eligible first-time buyers.

programs.name: MassHousing DPA Option 2
programs.notes: 2% fixed, repaid over 15 years. A third option is $25,000 at 3% over 15 years.

Boston.name: Boston Home Center First-Time Homebuyer DPA
Boston.amountText: Up to 3% of price, max $50,000 (under 100% AMI); up to 2%, max $35,000 (101-135% AMI); 2% for deed-restricted homes
Boston.notes: Grant for current Boston residents; 0% deferred loan (mortgage + note since 2026-09-15) for non-residents, repaid on sale, transfer or refinance; listed as deferred conservatively. Covers down payment plus eligible closing costs. 1-3 family or condo in Boston, owner-occupied; CHAPA Homebuying 101 and participating lender required. First-time = no ownership in 3 years.

Worcester.name: CDBG Down Payment Assistance
Worcester.notes: City Housing Development Division, CDBG-funded, for down payment and/or closing costs. 3-year residency restriction; city document does not state whether it is a grant or forgivable loan, so listed as deferred conservatively. Apply at least 45 days before closing; first-time homebuyer course required.

Springfield.name: Down Payment and Closing Cost Assistance
Springfield.notes: 0% forgivable loan per the city application (updated 2026-03-17): nothing forgiven in years 1-5, then 20% per year in years 6-10; prorated repayment on sale, refinance or transfer. Minimum 1% buyer funds, max 103% LTV, homebuyer education; 1-4 units. City web page (2022) still says $10,000-$20,000.

Cambridge.name: Down Payment Assistance
Cambridge.notes: Forgivable loan for down payment and closing costs; 20% forgiven per year over 5 years of owner occupancy. Single-family, condo, 2- or 3-family in Cambridge; first-time homebuyer workshop required.

programs.name: 1st Time Advantage 6000
programs.notes: 0% deferred 30-year second for down payment and closing costs, repaid when the first mortgage ends (sale, refinance, payoff). Paired with an MMP 1st Time Advantage first mortgage. First-time rule waived in targeted areas and for eligible veterans. Eligible for Partner Match.

programs.name: Flex 6000
programs.notes: Replaced Flex 5000. 0% second lien, no payments; due when the first mortgage ends. First-time or repeat buyers. Eligible for Partner Match.

programs.name: Flex 3%
programs.notes: 0% deferred second equal to exactly 3% of the first mortgage, due when the first mortgage ends. Repeat buyers allowed but may not own other real property at closing.

programs.name: First Homes for First Responders and Teachers
programs.notes: Launched Sept 2026. First mortgage rate 0.50% below MMP 1st Time Advantage 5%. At least one borrower must work in Maryland as an EMT, firefighter, police officer or teacher.

programs.name: House Keys 4 Employees (State of Maryland staff)
programs.amountText: Extra $2,500 on top of the $6,000 DPA ($8,500 total)
programs.notes: Active State of Maryland employees (permanent or contractual). 0% deferred; needs a 1st Time Advantage 6000 or Flex 6000 loan and homebuyer education.

programs.name: 1st Time Advantage 5%
programs.notes: 0% deferred second, due when the first mortgage ends. Min credit 640 per 2022 MMP quick reference; some products require more.

programs.name: 1st Time Advantage 3%
programs.notes: 0% deferred second, due when the first mortgage ends.

programs.name: HomeStart
programs.notes: Part of the 1st Time Advantage line. 0% deferred 30-year second, due on sale, transfer or payoff. Not combinable with Partner Match.

programs.name: Partner Match
programs.amountText: Matches partner (employer, builder, local government) DPA up to $2,500
programs.notes: 0% deferred state loan, due when the first mortgage is paid off. Only with 1st Time Advantage 6000 or Flex 6000 and assistance from an MMP-approved partner.

Baltimore City.name: Buying Into Baltimore
Baltimore City.notes: 20 winners per Trolley Tour lottery; no income limit, repeat buyers OK. Must attend a Live Baltimore Trolley Tour, complete counseling and contribute $1,000; fixed-rate mortgages only.

Baltimore City.name: Baybrook Boost
Baltimore City.amountText: $10,000, plus $5,000 Live Near Your Park bonus on select blocks (up to $15,000)
Baltimore City.notes: 0% deferred loan; repayment terms are in GBA's terms and conditions. FHA loans currently cannot be combined. First-time buyers not required.

Baltimore City.name: First-Time Homebuyer Incentive Program (FTHIP)
Baltimore City.amountText: 2.5% of price toward down payment, up to 50% of closing costs, possible GAP funding and rate buydown (amount varies)
Baltimore City.notes: City says most incentives are forgiven after 5 years in the home, but FTHIP terms are not spelled out, so shown as deferred. First-come, first-served; about $443k left on 11/16/2026.

Baltimore City.name: Baltimore City Employee Homeownership Program
Baltimore City.notes: City and quasi-City agency employees with 6+ months of service. City says most incentives are forgiven after 5 years, but terms not confirmed per program, so shown as deferred. 62 awards left on 11/16/2026.

Baltimore City.name: Vacants to Value Booster
Baltimore City.notes: For homes that were vacant 1+ year (Vacant Building Notice) and have a new Certificate of Occupancy. Shown as deferred because forgiveness terms are not stated per program. 42 awards left on 11/16/2026.

Baltimore City.name: Live Near Your Work
Baltimore City.notes: Grant for employees of participating employers buying near work. max is the city's share only.

Montgomery County.name: Revolving Closing Cost Assistance (RCCAP "5 for 5")
Montgomery County.agency: Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County
Montgomery County.notes: Repaid monthly at 5% over 10 years. Requires an HOC first mortgage; at least one borrower must work in Montgomery County.

Montgomery County.name: MPP Option 2
Montgomery County.agency: Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County
Montgomery County.notes: 0% deferred second with an HOC first mortgage; prorated repayment only if sold or paid off within 5 years.

Montgomery County.name: Montgomery Homeownership Program
Montgomery County.notes: 0% deferred second with an MMP first mortgage, due on sale, refinance, transfer or at 30 years. County says MHP and MEDPAL funding is currently limited.

Montgomery County.name: McHAF (MPP Option 3)
Montgomery County.agency: Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County
Montgomery County.notes: 0% deferred second with an HOC first mortgage; prorated repayment if sold or paid off within 10 years.

Montgomery County.name: Montgomery Employee Down Payment Assistance Loan (MEDPAL)
Montgomery County.agency: Montgomery County DHCA / Maryland Mortgage Program
Montgomery County.incomeNote: MMP and county Workforce Housing income limits
Montgomery County.notes: Approved Montgomery County Government employees. 0% second, due on sale, transfer or refinance; forgiven at 30 years. Borrower must put in 1% of price. Funding currently limited.

Howard County.name: Settlement Downpayment Loan Program
Howard County.amountText: Amount set by county (not published on program page)
Howard County.notes: Deferred; due on sale, refinance or default. Interest 2 points below the first mortgage rate (2024 changes cap it at 3%). Loan types: HomeStarter, HomeSteader and DreamMaker (first-time buyers) plus Revitalization and Workforce Initiative. Needs $1,000 own funds and a fixed-rate first mortgage. Funds limited, first come first served.

Prince George's County.name: Pathway to Purchase
Prince George's County.notes: 0% deferred loan for down payment, closing costs or principal reduction; recapture declines over a 15-year affordability period and the loan is forgiven after 15 years. Fixed-rate FHA or conventional first mortgage. Funds first come, first ready.

Anne Arundel County.name: Mortgage Assistance Program (MAP)
Anne Arundel County.notes: 0% deferred loan, due on sale, transfer, end of owner occupancy or 30 years. Use with an FHA or Maryland Mortgage Program first mortgage. Requires ACDS counseling and 1% own funds; no credit score minimum.

programs.name: Advantage Down Payment
programs.notes: $5,000 toward cash to close with a MaineHousing First Home Loan (no second mortgage); not available with the 2-point option. Requires a hoMEworks class and a 1% borrower contribution.

programs.name: Multi-Unit Advantage
programs.notes: For 2–4 unit owner-occupied homes with a First Home, Purchase Plus Improvement or Salute ME loan. No second mortgage, no rate add-on. 1% borrower contribution (may be a gift); homebuyer and landlord education required. Not available with Rural Development.

programs.name: Salute ME / Salute Home Again
programs.notes: For active duty, honorably discharged and retired military (180 days active duty or war-zone service). Includes the $5,000 Advantage plus 0.50% off the First Home Loan 30-year rate. Salute Home Again waives the first-time rule for returning homebuyers. hoMEworks class required.

programs.name: First Generation Program
programs.amountText: $10,000 grant toward closing costs + 1.00% rate discount
programs.notes: For lifetime first-time buyers who never lived in a home owned by their parents/guardians (or were in foster care); 1% borrower contribution plus financial-literacy and homebuyer classes. Can't combine with Salute ME or the 2-point option.

Bangor.name: Bangor Down Payment Assistance Program
Bangor.agency: City of Bangor Community & Economic Development
Bangor.amountText: Amount not published — contact the city
Bangor.incomeNote: Income-qualified (CDBG limits); home must be within Bangor city limits
Bangor.notes: CDBG-funded, first come first served. Amount, loan structure and first-time rule not stated on the city page; type set to deferred conservatively. Call (207) 992-4280.

Bangor.name: Bangor Closing Cost Assistance Program
Bangor.agency: City of Bangor Community & Economic Development
Bangor.amountText: Covers closing fees (appraisal, credit, title, flood cert, attorney, recording); amount not published
Bangor.notes: CDBG-funded, first come first served. Structure not stated; type set to deferred conservatively.

programs.name: MI 10K DPA
programs.incomeNote: Household income and purchase-price limits apply (statewide since May 8, 2023; formerly limited to 236 ZIP codes)
programs.notes: Available statewide; homebuyer education class required. Paired with an MSHDA first mortgage.

Detroit.name: Detroit Down Payment Assistance
Detroit.agency: City of Detroit Housing & Revitalization Dept.
Detroit.notes: City page confirms up to $25,000 and no home owned in past 3 years. Round 3 launched under Mayor Sheffield, funded with ~$9M CDBG/CDBG-DR. Grant vs loan terms not stated on the city page — shown conservatively as deferred.
Detroit.incomeNote: Detroit resident 12+ months (or lost Detroit home to tax foreclosure 2010–2016); income limits apply (2026: $58,700 for 1 to $110,700 for 8 per program partner)

Detroit.name: Wayne County DPA (National Faith)
Detroit.notes: 0% second mortgage forgiven after 5 years' occupancy; existing homes; no real estate owned in past 3 years. Wayne County outside the City of Detroit — Detroit itself is excluded (Detroit buyers use det-dpa). PAUSED: National Faith budget table (updated Sept 9, 2026) shows $0 remaining for Wayne County; first-come, first-served when refunded. Amount corrected from $14,999.

Grand Rapids.name: Homebuyer Assistance Fund
Grand Rapids.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI; assets ≤$10,000; price at/below HUD limits
Grand Rapids.notes: Up to $7,500 for down payment, closing costs and prepaids via participating lenders. No home owned in past 3 years; must occupy 5 years. City page does not say grant vs forgivable — shown conservatively as deferred.

Warren.name: Direct Homebuyer Assistance
Warren.amountText: Half the required down payment + up to $3,500 closing costs, max $25,000 (based on need)
Warren.notes: HOME-funded forgivable deferred-payment second mortgage, fully forgiven after a 5-year affordability period (2026 policy; the 2024 policy's 5/10-yr split by amount no longer appears). City-owned properties only — city page (updated Oct 28, 2026) lists 2 new-construction homes at 22708 and 22728 Mac Arthur. Requires 30-yr fixed-rate, fully amortizing first mortgage within 100 bps of Freddie Mac average; housing DTI ≤30%, total ≤45%. May add subsidy if PITI exceeds 30% of income. Specific loan types not restricted beyond fixed-rate. Very limited volume. Terms from HOME DPA Policies & Procedures (July 2026), linked from the city page.
Warren.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI ($58,700 for 1 to $110,700 for 8, HUD June 2026); must not currently own a home

programs.name: Monthly Payment Loan
programs.notes: Same rate as the first mortgage, repaid over 10 years. Works with Start Up (first-time) and Step Up (repeat) loans; no separate income limit.

programs.name: Deferred Payment Loan
programs.notes: 0% balloon loan due at sale, refinance, move-out or first-mortgage payoff. Start Up (first-time buyers) only.

programs.name: Deferred Payment Loan Plus
programs.notes: 0% deferred; for Start Up borrowers who meet the DPL Plus targeting criteria.

programs.name: First Place CashAssistance
programs.notes: 0% forgivable second equal to 4% of the first mortgage; starts reducing by 1/60 a month after year 5, gone at year 10. First-time buyers (no ownership in 3 years) or qualified veterans; waived in targeted tracts. Must repay if you sell or refinance within 10 years. Min credit 640 (660 manufactured).

programs.name: Next Step CashAssistance
programs.notes: Higher income limits than First Place. 0% forgivable second equal to 4% of the first mortgage over 10 years; up to 50% DTI. MHDC says Next Step serves first-time and repeat buyers, but its 2025-26 program documents list 'first-time homebuyer or qualified veteran' as a requirement for the cash assistance; confirm with a lender.

Springfield.name: Down Payment Assistance
Springfield.incomeNote: ≤80% Springfield median income; city limits; price ≤ $214,000
Springfield.notes: 0% loan, no payments, forgiven over 10 years as primary residence. First-time buyers and certain displaced persons. City's Home Buyer Assistance page says the program is temporarily paused.

Columbia.name: Homeownership Assistance
Columbia.notes: 0% forgivable loan for down payment, closing costs or principal reduction; prorated repayment if sold or rented within 10 years. Buyer contributes $500. Min average credit 600.

St. Louis City.name: HomeSTL
St. Louis City.amountText: Up to $40,000; up to $50,000 in Qualified Census Tracts
St. Louis City.notes: ARPA-funded 0% forgivable second (5, 10 or 15 years by amount). All funds fully reserved as of 8/31/2026 and reservations ended 9/30/2026; waiting list only. May not return.

St. Louis County.name: First Home Down Payment Loan
St. Louis County.agency: St. Louis County Office of Community Development
St. Louis County.amountText: Amount not confirmed (county page could not be read)
St. Louis County.notes: HOME-funded county program for St. Louis County buyers. Terms could not be confirmed, so shown as deferred; check with the county.
St. Louis County.source: St. Louis County program page title in search results (Nov 2026); page unreadable

Kansas City.name: Employee Homeownership Assistance Program
Kansas City.amountText: Up to 20% of price for down payment (max $30,000) plus up to $5,000 closing costs
Kansas City.notes: City employees buying inside KCMO limits. City describes it as a partial-forgiveness loan; forgiveness terms not published, so shown as deferred. Pilot funded with $750,000 (2024); current availability not confirmed. KCMO has no general city DPA program.

programs.name: Smart7
programs.notes: 0% second mortgage, due at sale, refinance, move-out or first-mortgage payoff. No first-time-buyer requirement. Credit per servicer guidelines.

programs.name: Easy8
programs.notes: 0% second, due at refinance, move-out or first-mortgage payoff. First-time rule (no ownership in 3 years) waived in Target Areas and for veterans. Homebuyer education required.

programs.name: Trusty10
programs.notes: 2% second mortgage repaid over 15 years. First-time rule waived in target areas and for veterans. Mississippi REALTORS® adds $2,000 more ("Trusty 10 Plus 2") while funds last.

programs.name: Housing Assistance for Teachers
programs.amountText: Up to $6,000 (borrower funds needed to close)
programs.notes: Mississippi Department of Education grant for full-time licensed public school teachers; forgiven after 3 years teaching in a critical teacher-shortage district. Home must be in the county where you teach. 1% own-funds contribution (not gifted) and 1 month reserves. 2026-2027 program live; subject to availability.
programs.incomeNote: No income limit unless combined with another MHC product

programs.name: Home4All
programs.notes: HOME-funded; MHC describes it as a grant (amount based on need) subject to an affordability period whose length isn't stated, so shown as deferred conservatively. No ownership in past 3 years; HUD-approved homebuyer education required. Assistance can’t exceed 50% of the price; county price limits.

Jackson.name: City of Jackson Homebuyer Assistance Program
Jackson.agency: City of Jackson Office of Housing and Community Development
Jackson.notes: HOME-funded DPA delivered through city-funded nonprofits; home must be in Jackson city limits and kept as primary residence for an affordability period (length not stated), so shown as deferred conservatively. 8-hour homebuyer education required; funds limited to open application periods.

programs.name: Bond Advantage DPA
programs.notes: 15-year amortizing second at the same fixed rate as the MBOH first mortgage. Requires an MBOH Regular Bond 30-year first mortgage (FHA, VA, USDA-RD or HUD-184), which is aimed at first-time buyers; $1,000 minimum borrower cash (may be gifted); homebuyer education required. Due on sale/transfer or refinance.

programs.name: MBOH Plus 0% Deferred DPA
programs.notes: 0% deferred 30-year second, no payments; due on sale/transfer, refinance or payoff of the first loan (no forgiveness). Max 45% DTI; $1,000 minimum borrower cash; homebuyer education required. Requires MBOH Regular Bond 30-year fixed first mortgage (FHA, VA, USDA-RD or HUD-184), aimed at first-time buyers.

Billings.name: Billings First Time Homebuyer Program
Billings.notes: 0% interest deferred-payment loan; forgiveness not stated. Homebuyer education required. City says funding available as of Sept 10, 2026, first-come first-served.

programs.name: NC Home Advantage DPA
programs.notes: 0% deferred second, forgiven 20% a year in years 11–15. First-time and move-up buyers. Repay only if you sell, refinance or transfer before year 15. Min credit 640 (660 manufactured homes). Paired with NC Home Advantage Mortgage (FHA, VA, USDA or conventional).
programs.incomeNote: Income up to $158,000; sales price limits follow the first-mortgage loan type

programs.name: NC 1st Home Advantage Down Payment
programs.notes: 0% deferred second, forgiven 20% a year in years 11–15. First-time buyers (no principal residence in 3 yrs), military veterans, or homes in targeted census tracts. Min credit 640 (660 manufactured). Paired with NC Home Advantage Mortgage; offered as an alternative to the 3% option.
programs.incomeNote: Income and sales-price limits per NCHFA spreadsheet (not checked)

programs.name: Community Partners Loan Pool (CPLP)
programs.amountText: Up to 25% of price, max $50,000 (min $5,000) with NC Home Advantage Mortgage; up to 10% with USDA 502 Direct
programs.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI (HUD HOME limits) with sales-price limits
programs.notes: 0% deferred subordinate loan, term matches first mortgage (up to 30 yrs; 33 with USDA 502 Direct); repaid on sale or default, no forgiveness stated; 5–10 yr affordability period. Must pair with NC Home Advantage Mortgage or USDA 502 Direct. Apply through a participating CPLP member (local nonprofit/government). 6 hrs homebuyer education + 2 hrs one-on-one counseling. Per Jan 2026 guidelines; fund availability varies by member.

Charlotte.name: House Charlotte
Charlotte.agency: City of Charlotte (administered by DreamKey Partners)
Charlotte.amountText: Up to $80,000 (Program 1A, ≤80% AMI: $30K base + match up to $50K); up to $30,000 for 80–110% AMI (1B: $10K base + match up to $20K, or 1B Exemption $30K)
Charlotte.incomeNote: Up to 110% AMI ($129,150; 1A ≤80% AMI $93,900); max price $365,000; Charlotte city limits
Charlotte.notes: 0% deferred, 30-year term, forgiven at year 31 per City of Charlotte tier table. 1B match waived (1B Exemption) for City of Charlotte, Mecklenburg County and CMS employees. 8 hrs HUD-approved homebuyer education required; lender applies on buyer's behalf; can combine with NCHFA CPLP. DreamKey warns funding is limited. Credit minimum and eligible first-mortgage types not stated — loan types kept from prior data.

Raleigh.name: Homebuyer Assistance Program
Raleigh.amountText: Up to $45,000 (Standard); up to $60,000 (Enhanced, targeted areas)
Raleigh.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI ($105,850 for 4). Price cap $389,500 Standard (page also cites $384,750) / $450,000 Enhanced
Raleigh.notes: 0% interest deferred loan; no payments until the home is sold or is no longer the primary residence. Not forgivable. Enhanced carries a 10-year deed restriction limiting resale proceeds. Through City-approved lenders; credit minimum and first-mortgage types not stated.

Greensboro.name: Housing Connect Homebuyer Assistance
Greensboro.amountText: Up to $15,000 ($20,000 in redevelopment/reinvestment areas) per secondary source; not confirmed on the City's site
Greensboro.source: City of Greensboro program page (eligibility only); amounts from The Mortgage Reports state guide (Nov 2026)
Greensboro.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI standard; 80–120% AMI under Public Service Heroes / #100Homes
Greensboro.notes: City page (re-checked 2026-11-27) confirms the program with Standard (≤80% AMI), Public Service Heroes and #100Homes (80–120% AMI) offerings, first-time rule (or no home owned in 3 yrs), Greensboro city limits, and a bonus in 8 redevelopment/reinvestment areas (Dudley Heights, Eastside Park, Glenwood, Kings Forest, Mill District, Ole Asheboro, Random Woods, Willow Oaks). It does not state amounts or loan terms; amounts are from a secondary source and city news/guideline pages could not be reached. Secondary source describes it as forgivable over 10 years; modeled conservatively as deferred until confirmed.

Durham.name: City of Durham Down Payment Assistance
Durham.amountText: Up to $80,000 (25% of price, capped at $80,000)
Durham.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI ($101,700 for 4, FY2026); price ≤95% of HUD area max; City of Durham only
Durham.notes: 0% forgivable second, forgiven 1/15 per year of occupancy over 15 years (per Aug 2024 guidelines). No home owned in past 3 years. 30-yr fixed FHA/VA/conventional first mortgage; USDA not supported. $1,000 buyer contribution. First-come, first-served until $3.2M is depleted; approved lender list dated July 2026.

programs.name: Start
programs.incomeNote: Low-to-moderate income; higher limits than DCA
programs.notes: Credit at closing secured by a second lien with no separate payment; lien terminates after 96 monthly mortgage payments (8 years). Pro-rated balance repaid if sold, refinanced or transferred earlier. Paired with FirstHome, HomeAccess or ND Roots (repeat buyers OK via ND Roots); first-mortgage rate is higher than with DCA. 1–2 unit homes; $500 borrower cash; cannot combine with other DPA. Terms per NDHFA program training (May 2026).

programs.name: Down Payment and Closing Cost Assistance (DCA)
programs.incomeNote: Lower-income limits by county/household size (e.g., Cass 4-person $92,150, eff. 7/15/2026)
programs.notes: Same structure as Start: second lien, no separate payment, satisfied after 96 monthly payments; pro-rated repayment if sold/refinanced earlier. Paired with FirstHome (first-time) or HomeAccess (single parents, veterans, disabled/65+); first-mortgage rate matches FirstHome Standard. Homebuyer education required before closing. 1–2 unit homes; cannot combine with other DPA.

programs.name: Homebuyer Assistance (HBA)
programs.incomeNote: First Home program limits by county/household size
programs.notes: Amortizing 1% 10-year second paired with a NIFA First Home first mortgage (higher first-loan rate). First-time = no primary residence in past 3 years; homebuyer education required. Min credit score applies (not published on HBA page).

programs.name: Welcome Home Assistance (WHA)
programs.notes: Amortizing 1% 10-year second paired with a NIFA Welcome Home first mortgage; open to first-time and repeat buyers. 640 min score (max DTI 45%; 50% at 660+). First-time buyers need homebuyer education. 1–2 unit homes.

Omaha.name: City of Omaha Homebuyer Assistance (Omaha 100)
Omaha.agency: Omaha 100, Inc. for City of Omaha HCD
Omaha.notes: City-funded down payment assistance, low-interest loans and City-backed second mortgages administered by Omaha 100; housing education/counseling required. Terms not published; type set conservatively to deferred.

Lincoln.name: Lincoln First Time Home Buyer Program
Lincoln.agency: NeighborWorks Lincoln / City of Lincoln Urban Development
Lincoln.amountText: Varies by price and household income — amount not published
Lincoln.notes: Down payment, closing cost and limited rehab assistance for existing homes inside Lincoln city limits; extra incentives in priority neighborhoods. No ownership in past 3 years (exceptions possible); NeighborWorks Lincoln homebuyer training required. Repayment terms not published; type set conservatively to deferred.

programs.name: Down Payment & Closing Cost Assistance
programs.incomeNote: Limits vary by program (up to $184,500 for Flex Plus / Preferred Plus over 80% AMI)
programs.notes: 0% second mortgage, no payments, 30-year term; due in full on sale, refinance, bankruptcy, move-out or at 30 years (not forgiven). Requires an NH Housing first mortgage and NH Housing homebuyer education.

programs.name: 1stGenHomeNH
programs.notes: Limited-funding pilot for first-generation buyers (you, your parents/guardians and non-borrowing spouse never owned; foster care, refugee or asylum status also qualifies), on top of standard NH Housing assistance. Requires an NH Housing loan and face-to-face education (AHEAD, HOMEteam or Housing Partnership). Terms not published — shown as deferred; NH Housing may end it anytime.

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.agency: NJ Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency (NJHMFA)

programs.name: NJHMFA Down Payment Assistance
programs.amountText: Up to $15,000 (amount depends on the property's county)
programs.notes: Interest-free second loan, no monthly payments, forgiven after 5 years. Must be paired with an NJHMFA 30-year fixed first mortgage (First-Time Homebuyer/Homeward Bound: FHA/VA/USDA; HFA Advantage: conventional). First-time = no ownership in prior 3 years. Min credit 620 (NJHMFA program highlights, updated 10/19/2026). Income and purchase-price limits apply (higher in Urban Target Areas).

programs.name: First Generation DPA
programs.notes: $7,000 on top of the NJHMFA DPA (combined $17,000-$22,000 depending on county). Interest-free, forgiven after 5 years. First-generation = parents/guardians hold no residential ownership interest (or buyer was ever in NJ foster care), plus no ownership in prior 3 years. Requires an NJHMFA 30-year fixed first mortgage; min credit 620.

Camden County.name: First Time Homebuyer Program
Camden County.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI (HUD HOME limits; $91,750 for 4 per county page, June 2024 figures)
Camden County.notes: 0% non-amortizing forgivable loan for down payment (up to 5%), closing costs and principal write-down. Term is 5 years for awards under $15,000 and 10 years for $15,000-$25,000; repayable if sold during the term. Excludes Camden City, Tavistock and Pine Valley (Camden City buyers use the city's own program). Not owned a home in past 3 years (single parents/displaced homemakers excepted). Fixed-rate first mortgage of 30 years or less required; no program credit-score minimum. Contact FTHBP@camdencounty.com / (856) 751-2242. Rate/term details from the county's 2024 Policies & Procedures (the current version linked from the program page).

Gloucester County.name: Homebuyer Down Payment Assistance
Gloucester County.notes: 0% deferred payment loan; funds go to closing costs first, then down payment. 5-10 year affordability period with full repayment on sale/refinance; the county describes partial (1/5 per year) forgiveness afterward but the wording is ambiguous, so treated conservatively as deferred. No home ownership in past 3 years. Requires 3% buyer investment and 8 hours of HUD-approved homebuyer education. Pre-apply online or call (856) 384-6930.

Newark / Essex County.name: Essex County Homebuyer Assistance Program (HAP)
Newark / Essex County.amountText: Up to $50,000 (per 2022 county brochure; call (973) 655-0200 ext. 322 to confirm)
Newark / Essex County.source: Essex County HAP brochure dated 11/30/2022 (agency doc >1 year old); no newer county page found 2026-11-27
Newark / Essex County.notes: No-interest deferred HOME loan for down payment, closing costs or mortgage write-down; 15-year lien. Only the 19 Essex County Consortium towns (e.g., Belleville, Bloomfield, Montclair, Nutley, Orange, West Orange) - NOT Newark, East Orange or Irvington. Price caps in 2022: $309k (1-unit), $395k (2-unit), $479k (3-unit).

Newark / Essex County.name: Live Newark Closing Cost Program
Newark / Essex County.notes: 0% forgivable loan for first-time buyers purchasing in Newark; 20% forgiven per full year over 5 years.

Newark / Essex County.name: Live Newark Municipal Employee Housing
Newark / Essex County.notes: For City of Newark employees buying in Newark. No-interest forgivable loan described as similar to the Closing Cost Program, but the forgiveness schedule isn't stated, so it's treated conservatively as deferred. First-time requirement not stated.

Jersey City.name: First Time Homebuyer Program
Jersey City.agency: City of Jersey City Division of Community Development
Jersey City.amountText: Up to 10% of price for down payment + $10,000 closing costs, max $150,000
Jersey City.source: City of Jersey City press release, Oct 17 2025 (agency doc >1 year old); City affordable-housing page (2026-11-27) gives no window
Jersey City.notes: HOME-funded subsidy the city calls a grant, but it is recaptured if the buyer sells, moves or defaults during an unstated affordability period, so it's treated as deferred. PAUSED: awarded by lottery; the current list (1,600+ applicants) is being served and a new application window will open only when it's exhausted. Requires 8 hours of HUD-approved education. Call 201-547-6910.

Middlesex County.name: American Dream Downpayment Program
Middlesex County.agency: Middlesex County Division of Housing, Community Development & Social Services
Middlesex County.amountText: $5,000 for down payment and closing costs
Middlesex County.incomeNote: County page lists $69,700 for 4; price ≤4× household income, max $304,000 (figures look dated — confirm at 732-745-3025)
Middlesex County.notes: Deferred-repayment mortgage; no principal or interest due if the buyer owns and occupies the home for 5 years. First-time buyers who have lived in Middlesex County ≥1 year. Excludes New Brunswick and Perth Amboy. 1% buyer contribution, mortgage pre-approval within 2 months, in-person homebuyer course and HUD-approved counseling. Rate, credit minimum and first-mortgage types not stated; application window not stated.

Bergen County.name: American Dream First Time Homebuyer Program
Bergen County.agency: Bergen County Division of Community Development
Bergen County.amountText: Up to $55,000 second mortgage + up to $10,000 down-payment match (per 2024 county brochure)
Bergen County.incomeNote: ≤80% of county median income; price ≤95% of Bergen County median sales price
Bergen County.source: Bergen County program page (status) + 2024 American Dream brochure (agency doc >1 year old)
Bergen County.notes: PAUSED: county page says the program is on hold until further notice and has not taken applications since January 2025. When running: 0% second mortgage deferred until sale or title change; the match converts to a grant after 10 years. First-time or no ownership in past 3 years. Contact (201) 336-7206.

programs.name: FIRSTDown
programs.notes: Low fixed-rate second mortgage with 10-, 15- or 30-year terms; must be paired with a FirstHome loan. All Housing New Mexico assistance combined is capped at $35,000.

programs.name: FirstDown Plus
programs.notes: 0% loan, no payments, forgiven in year 11; down payment only (not closing costs). Requires a FirstHome loan; funds first come, first served.

programs.name: HOMENow
programs.notes: 0% second with a 10-year affordability period; paired with a FirstHome loan. Funds limited, first come first served.

programs.name: Home Is Possible for First-Time Homebuyers
programs.notes: 0% interest, no-payment, non-forgivable 30-year second mortgage. 2% or 4% option (higher first-mortgage rate with 4%). No ownership in past 3 years. 640 min credit (660 manufactured). Homebuyer education required. Listed on Nov 25, 2026 rate sheet.
programs.incomeNote: County income/price limits; conventional ≤ 80% AMI, price ≤ $570,000

programs.name: Home First
programs.incomeNote: Price ≤ $570,000; income ≤ 300% of Federal Poverty Level (FHA/VA/USDA)
programs.notes: Down payment only (not closing costs). Forgiven after 3 years in the home. 640 min credit (680 manufactured). 6 months Nevada residency and homebuyer education required. Status uncertain: not on the Nov 25, 2026 HIP rate sheet, and the main-site Home First URL now shows the general Home Is Possible page; only the legacy d9 page still describes it. Confirm with a HIP lender.

programs.name: Home Is Possible
programs.notes: No first-time-buyer requirement. 0% no-payment, non-forgivable 30-year second mortgage; 3% or 5% option (higher first-mortgage rate with 5%). Conventional options for ≤80% AMI and over-80% AMI (≤ $165,000). 640 min credit (660 manufactured). Homebuyer education required.

programs.name: HIP for Teachers
programs.notes: Licensed full-time K–12 public (rate sheet also says charter) school classroom teachers in Nevada. 0% no-payment note, prorated forgiveness over 5 years. Available through Dec 31, 2026. Page metadata mentions $10,000 but body and rate sheet say $7,500. Nov 2026 rate sheet lists FHA/VA/USDA-RD and conventional options.

programs.name: Launchpad (Nevada Rural Housing)
programs.incomeNote: Income ≤ $165,000; rural Nevada only (excludes Reno, Las Vegas, Henderson, North Las Vegas and urban Clark/Washoe townships)
programs.notes: 0% deferred second mortgage, never forgiven; due at sale, refinance, move-out or 30-year maturity. Min credit 640 (program page says 680 for manufactured homes). A first-time-buyer version offers 2% or 4% with county income/price limits. Rates as of Nov 23, 2026; check address at HALmap.org.

programs.name: Kickstart (Nevada Rural Housing)
programs.incomeNote: ≤ 80% AMI; Carson City, Douglas, Lyon, Storey and Washoe counties only (excludes Reno city limits)
programs.notes: 0% forgivable second mortgage, no payments; forgiven in full after 5 years (not prorated), repayable if sold or refinanced earlier. Plus 2% permanent rate reduction. Limited funding; active on Nov 23, 2026 rate page.

programs.name: Rural Rocks $20K (Nevada Rural Housing)
programs.incomeNote: ≤ 150% AMI by county (e.g. Clark $147,300, Washoe $175,200); price ≤ $832,750; rural Nevada incl. Clark/Washoe communities under 150,000 (excludes Reno, Las Vegas, Henderson, North Las Vegas, Enterprise, Paradise, Spring Valley, Sunrise Manor)
programs.notes: 0% no-payment second mortgage forgiven at the end of 30 years; due earlier on sale, refinance or move-out. Can fund a 2% rate buydown. 6 months Nevada residency; prior NRH program users ineligible. Rate page (Nov 23, 2026): fully reserved, waitlist open, cannot close until moved off the waitlist.

programs.name: Worker Advantage Program
programs.amountText: $20,000 (can instead fund 2% or 4% discount points, remainder to down payment/closing)
programs.notes: Essential workers (health care, education, public safety, construction labor) with 6 months Nevada residency; prior HIP recipients ineligible. 0% no-payment, non-forgivable 30-year second mortgage; $20,000 can instead buy 2% or 4% discount points, remainder to down payment/closing. FHA, VA, USDA-RD, Fannie HFA Preferred, Freddie HFA Advantage. $18M first-come revolving pool; not shown on the Nov 2026 HIP rate sheet, so availability should be confirmed. Min credit per HIP product (660 manufactured); confirmed via NHD press release (Dec 2025) and program administrator guide rev. 07/16/26.
