Las Vegas / Clark County.name: Culinary and Bartenders Housing Fund
Las Vegas / Clark County.agency: Culinary and Bartenders Housing Fund (Culinary Union Local 226)
Las Vegas / Clark County.notes: For workers covered by the Culinary/Bartenders union contract with 2,000+ hours over 3 years. 0% loan, no payments; repaid at face value on sale, rental or refinance (not forgiven). No ownership in past 3 years. Buyer contributes 3.5% (FHA) or 1% (conventional). 8-hour homebuyer class plus counseling. Funds limited, first come first served.

Reno / Washoe County.name: Alpine Vista Advantage (HIP)
Reno / Washoe County.notes: Washoe County only: down payment and closing-cost help for new homes in the Alpine Vista development, paired with a builder-funded 4% rate buydown (HIP rate sheet Nov 25, 2026). Repayment/forgiveness terms not stated; treated conservatively as deferred. Not available for other homes.

NY.name: New York
NY.agency: State of New York Mortgage Agency (SONYMA)

programs.name: SONYMA Down Payment Assistance Loan (DPAL)
programs.amountText: Greater of $3,000 or 3% of price, capped at $15,000 (min $1,000; cannot exceed actual down payment/closing costs)
programs.notes: 0% second lien, no payments, forgiven after 10 years (pro-rated 1/120 per month if sold/refinanced earlier). Only with a SONYMA first mortgage; first-mortgage rate is 0.40% higher with DPAL (except Graduate to Homeownership, Homes for Veterans, ENERGY STAR). Buyer must contribute 1% (3% co-ops/3-4 family). SONYMA programs require first-time buyers except veterans/Target Areas. Min credit score not published on HCR site; loan insurance types not stated on DPAL page.

programs.name: SONYMA DPAL Plus 2026
programs.amountText: Up to $30,000 (down payment, closing costs, single-premium MI)
programs.notes: Launched July 1, 2026; statewide via participating SONYMA lenders, first-come first-served until funds run out. HCR page does not publish forgiveness/repayment terms (refers to a separate term sheet), so typed conservatively as deferred. Must be applied after any other subsidies/grants.

programs.name: SONYMA Repayable Second Lien (RSL)
programs.amountText: Up to 5% of net purchase price (min $3,000; cannot exceed actual down payment/closing costs)
programs.notes: 0% interest, no monthly payments; repaid on sale, refinance or payoff of the SONYMA first mortgage. Alternative to DPAL (larger % but never forgiven). First-mortgage rate +0.40% (with same exceptions as DPAL).

programs.name: SONYMA Conventional Plus / FHA Plus
programs.amountText: Down payment & closing cost assistance included — amount not published on HCR page
programs.notes: 30-year fixed Conventional or FHA first mortgage bundled with SONYMA DPA; open to first-time and returning buyers. HCR page gives no DPA amount or forgiveness terms, so typed conservatively as deferred with amount unknown.

New York City.name: HomeFirst Down Payment Assistance
New York City.notes: Forgivable loan with owner-occupancy period of 10 years if ≤$40,000, 15 years if over $40,000 (City-funded loans: 15 years regardless). Buyer must contribute 3% of price; HPD-approved homebuyer education required; 1-4 family, condo or co-op in the five boroughs; price at or below 95% of HUD limits.

Buffalo.name: City of Buffalo Down Payment & Closing Cost Assistance (via Belmont)
Buffalo.agency: City of Buffalo / Belmont Housing Resources for WNY
Buffalo.amountText: Up to $15,000 for down payment and closing costs
Buffalo.notes: Listed on Belmont's First Time Homebuyer Programs page; apply through a Belmont counselor (716-884-7791). Structure, income limits and funding status not published, so typed conservatively as deferred.

Rochester.name: Home Purchase Assistance Program (HPAP)
Rochester.notes: City calls it a grant but requires 5 years of owner-occupancy, so modeled as forgivable over 5 years. 1-4 family homes in City of Rochester; buyer contributes $1,500; pre/post-purchase training required. First mortgage (Conventional, FHA, VA or SONYMA) of at least $25,000.

Westchester County.name: Westchester County Home Ownership Initiative
Westchester County.notes: All or part repayable if owner moves, sells or violates terms within the required occupancy period (period not legible on county page) — typed conservatively as deferred. House, condo or co-op in Westchester County; Yonkers eligibility not confirmed on the page. Funding status not stated.

Syracuse.name: Home HeadQuarters Closing Cost Assistance
Syracuse.incomeNote: 3% rate if <80% HUD median; up to 6% otherwise
Syracuse.notes: Amortizing loan repaid over 5 years at up to 6% simple interest (3% for <80% median income). Available anywhere in NY State except NYC; buyer must put $500 of own funds and complete homebuyer education.

Ithaca / Tompkins region.name: INHS Down Payment Assistance
Ithaca / Tompkins region.notes: For purchases in Cayuga, Chemung, Cortland, Schuyler, Seneca, Tioga or Tompkins counties. Structure not stated (typed conservatively as deferred); availability depends on grant funding.

programs.name: OHFA Down Payment Assistance
programs.notes: Formerly "Your Choice!". Forgiven after 7 years; repay it all if you sell sooner. FHA needs 650 credit; VA and USDA 640.

programs.name: Grants for Grads
programs.notes: For first-time buyers who earned a degree within the last 18 months; also a lower interest rate. Forgiven after 5 years if you stay in Ohio.

programs.name: Communities First Ohio DPA
programs.agency: Communities First Ohio (managed by The Port of Greater Cincinnati)
programs.amountText: 3%, 4% or 5% of the home, depending on rate option chosen
programs.incomeNote: Income limits based on borrower income (not household); separate limits for conventional and government loans
programs.notes: Grant: no second mortgage, no resale/refinance restrictions, no minimum occupancy period. Offered statewide through participating lenders. Min FICO 620 (subject to change). Eligible first mortgages listed as 'Govt. Loans' and Freddie Mac (LTV ≤97%); FHA/VA/USDA not named individually. First-time rule not stated. pct set to the 3% minimum; higher options carry a higher rate.

Columbus.name: American Dream Down Payment Initiative
Columbus.amountText: Up to 6% of purchase price or $14,999, whichever is less
Columbus.incomeNote: ≤120% AMI ($133,800 for 4, eff. 6/1/2026); home inside Columbus city limits; price may not exceed appraised value
Columbus.notes: Five-year deferred forgivable loan for down payment, closing costs or principal reduction; repay from net proceeds if sold, rented or transferred within 5 years. First-time = no ownership in past 36 months. No program minimum credit (lender decides); DTI caps 35%/45%. Fixed-rate first mortgages only (conventional, FHA, USDA, VA, 203K). Limited funds, first come first served. Guidelines updated 5/1/2026 (non-federal fund version).

Cleveland / Cuyahoga County.name: Cuyahoga County Down Payment Assistance Program
Cleveland / Cuyahoga County.agency: Cuyahoga County (administered by Believe Mortgage / CHN Housing Partners)
Cleveland / Cuyahoga County.amountText: Up to 10% of purchase price, max $20,900 (County page). Administrator's page cites up to 17% / $21,900; the lower County figures are used
Cleveland / Cuyahoga County.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI; single-family primary residence in one of 51 participating Cuyahoga urban-county communities. Excludes the cities of Cleveland, Cleveland Heights, East Cleveland, Euclid and Lakewood
Cleveland / Cuyahoga County.notes: Deferred, subordinated loan, repayable on sale, transfer or refinance. Believe Mortgage says it is forgivable after 5 or 10 years of owner occupancy depending on amount, but the County does not state forgiveness, so modeled as deferred. Buyer must not have owned a home in the last 3 years. Free homeownership classes required (CHN Housing Partners). Min credit and loan types not stated. Earlier '≤$149,000 home value' limit not confirmed and removed. Note: City of Cleveland homes are NOT eligible, and the City of Cleveland has no direct buyer DPA (only developer-side Single-Family Gap Financing). A separate Parma DPA has the same eligibility rules.

Cincinnati.name: American Dream Downpayment Initiative
Cincinnati.incomeNote: Low-to-moderate income (HOME/ADDI, ≤80% AMI); single-family owner-occupied home
Cincinnati.notes: Five-year 0% deferred loan, 20% forgiven per year of occupancy; recaptured if the buyer sells or moves within 5 years. First-time buyers, or no ownership in last 3 years. HUD-approved homebuyer counseling required. Administered directly by the City (Dept. of Community & Economic Development); 2026 Action Plan caps aid at $15,000 and projects 20 buyers; rolling applications. Min credit and loan types not stated.

programs.name: OHFA Homebuyer DPA
programs.notes: First-time and repeat buyers, all 77 counties; FHA, HUD-184, USDA, VA or conventional. Secured by a lien. Special rates for school employees, first responders and state employees.

programs.name: Flex Lending DPA
programs.notes: FirstHome (first-time) or NextStep (anyone income-eligible). Can cover 100% of cash to close and stack with other DPA. Above 80% AMI it’s a 30-year amortizing second at the first-mortgage rate + 1%.

programs.name: Keystone Advantage Assistance Loan
programs.amountText: Lesser of 4% of price/appraised value or $6,000 ($8,000 for participating Employer Assisted Housing employees)
programs.incomeNote: PHFA first-mortgage income limits apply; liquid assets max $50,000 after closing
programs.notes: 0% second mortgage repaid monthly over 10 years. Requires a PHFA first mortgage (Keystone Home, Keystone Government or HFA Preferred). Covers only minimum required down payment/closing costs; minimum $500. Cannot be combined with other PHFA DPA (except Access Modification).

programs.name: Keystone Forgivable in Ten Years (K-FIT)
programs.amountText: 5% of the lesser of price or appraised value, no dollar cap
programs.incomeNote: PHFA first-mortgage income limits apply; liquid assets max $50,000 after closing
programs.notes: Forgiven 10% per year over 10 years; prorated repayment on sale, transfer or non-owner occupancy. Only with Keystone Home Loan (or Keystone Flex). Covers only minimum required down payment/closing costs.

programs.name: Keystone Due At Time of Expiration (K-DATE)
programs.amountText: 8% of the lesser of price or appraised value for first mortgages up to $150,000 (subject to availability); 5% for first mortgages over $150,000; no dollar cap
programs.incomeNote: PHFA first-mortgage income limits apply; liquid assets max $50,000 after closing
programs.notes: Launched May 2026. 0% 30-year second mortgage, no monthly payments; due in full on sale, refinance or first-mortgage payoff. pct shows the 5% tier for loans over $150k; 8% tier for smaller loans. Keystone Home Loan / Keystone Flex only.

programs.name: HOMEstead DPA
programs.incomeNote: County-specific HOMEstead income and purchase price limits; not available in major cities/7 counties with their own HUD allocation
programs.notes: PHFA paused HOMEstead until further notice for reservations on or after Aug 7, 2026 (Q3 2026 program update). Was a 0% second forgiven 20%/yr over 5 years with Keystone Home Loan.

programs.name: Access Downpayment & Closing Cost Assistance (disability)
programs.incomeNote: Household income at or below 80% of statewide median family income
programs.notes: Buyer or household member with a disability; must also use the Access Home Modification Loan. 0% interest, no monthly payment; repaid on sale, transfer or non-owner occupancy. Not combinable with other PHFA DPA.

programs.name: PHFA Grant
programs.notes: Only with HFA Preferred (Lo MI) conventional first mortgage; can be combined with Keystone Advantage Assistance.

Philadelphia.name: Philly First Home
Philadelphia.incomeNote: Household income limits apply (e.g. $122,700 for a household of 4)
Philadelphia.notes: Described as a grant, but must be repaid if the buyer moves or refinances before living in the home 15 years (city page does not describe proration). First-time = no ownership in 3 years. City-funded counseling required before signing agreement of sale. Single-family or duplex; no condos. Offered while funding is available. Loan types not specified by the city.

Pittsburgh.name: Down Payment and Closing Cost Assistance Program
Pittsburgh.amountText: Up to $7,500 (under 80% AMI) or up to $5,000 (80-115% AMI)
Pittsburgh.notes: 0% deferred loan, not a grant: 5-year term (<80% AMI) or 10-year (80-115% AMI), no payments if residency met; URA does not state forgiveness explicitly, so typed conservatively as deferred. City of Pittsburgh only; HUD-certified homebuyer course; max $20,000 liquid assets after closing; 2% closing fee; apply 21 business days before closing.

Allegheny County (outside Pittsburgh).name: 1st Home Allegheny
Allegheny County (outside Pittsburgh).agency: Allegheny County Economic Development / Residential Finance Authority
Allegheny County (outside Pittsburgh).notes: Forgivable subordinate loan, 6-year term (county page does not detail forgiveness schedule). Excludes City of Pittsburgh. No home owned in last 3 years; buyer contributes $1,000 or 1% of price; assets under $40,000; 2 months reserves; HUD-certified education. Limited funding ($2.6M); page says accepting applications.

Bethlehem.name: Bethlehem Homebuyer Assistance Program (BHAP)
Bethlehem.agency: City of Bethlehem / Community Action Lehigh Valley
Bethlehem.amountText: Up to 10% of the financing plus closing costs; no dollar cap stated
Bethlehem.notes: 0% deferred loan forgiven gradually over 10 years; prorated repayment if not occupied 10 years. Buyer contributes $1,275 and completes counseling. City page gives no current open/closed status; confirm with CACLV. Allentown city has no direct homebuyer DPA program (per its Grants Dept).

programs.name: Statewide DPA Grant
programs.notes: The ARPA-funded $17,500 grant ($30M) helped about 1,600 buyers and is no longer listed among RIHousing’s current programs. Ask RIHousing whether new funding is coming.

programs.name: 15kDPA
programs.notes: 0% loan, no monthly payments; due when you sell, refinance or move out. Needs a RIHousing first mortgage and homebuyer education.

programs.name: Extra Assistance
programs.notes: Repayable second at the same rate as your RIHousing first mortgage. Homebuyer education required.

programs.name: FirstGenHomeRI
programs.notes: Pilot with limited funds, first come first served; RIHousing Loan Center only. First-generation buyers currently living in Central Falls, East Providence, Pawtucket, Woonsocket, Providence (not 02906) or Newport tract 405; can buy anywhere in RI. 0%, no payments; forgiven after 5 years of owner-occupancy.

programs.name: RI REALTORS® Homebuyer Grant
programs.notes: All available grant funds have been reserved. Requires a RIHousing first mortgage; stackable with other RIHousing assistance.

Providence.name: Providence Down Payment & Closing Cost Assistance
Providence.agency: City of Providence Dept. of Housing & Human Services
Providence.amountText: Per-buyer amount not yet announced ($550,000 HOME-funded program)
Providence.notes: Approved May 2026 in the city's 2026-27 HUD plan: forgivable purchase loans for first-time buyers. Administrator, per-buyer amount and forgiveness period not yet published — contact Housing & Human Services (401-680-8400). Providence residents may also qualify for RIHousing's FirstGenHomeRI.

programs.name: Palmetto Home Advantage
programs.notes: Forgivable, no monthly payment. First-time, move-up and repeat buyers in all 46 counties; no price limit.

programs.name: Palmetto Heroes
programs.notes: For teachers, law enforcement, firefighters, EMS, nurses, correctional officers, veterans, active duty and National Guard. Funded in yearly rounds — check whether this year’s round is open.

programs.name: Fixed Rate Plus
programs.incomeNote: First-Time program: SD Housing income limits, price ≤$410,000; Repeat program: income <$124,080 (1–2) / <$144,760 (3+), price ≤$460,000
programs.notes: 0% second mortgage, no monthly payments, due on sale or refinance; first-mortgage rate slightly higher. Offered with both the First-Time and Repeat Homebuyer programs (repeat program min credit 620).

programs.name: Give Me Five
programs.incomeNote: First-Time Homebuyer program income limits; price ≤$410,000
programs.notes: New limited-time program launched Nov 2, 2026: second mortgage, no monthly payments, forgiven after 5 years of owner occupancy. No ownership in past 3 years. Apply through participating lenders; eligible first-mortgage types not stated (SD Housing offers FHA, VA, USDA-RD, conventional).

Sioux Falls.name: Public Safety Down Payment Assistance
Sioux Falls.amountText: Up to $20,000 or 20% of price, whichever is less
Sioux Falls.incomeNote: No income limit stated; price ≤$385,000 (adjusted annually by FHFA HPI)
Sioux Falls.notes: For full-time certified law enforcement or fire rescue employees (1+ year) buying in designated Sioux Falls neighborhoods; no payments, forgiven after 5 years of owner occupancy. First-mortgage types not stated.

programs.name: Great Choice — Deferred
programs.notes: 0% Great Choice Plus second, forgiven after 10 years; due in full if you sell or refinance sooner. Homebuyer education required. Requires a THDA Great Choice first mortgage: FHA, USDA-RD or Freddie Mac HFA Advantage conventional; VA only via Homeownership for Heroes. First-time buyers, except repeat buyers in 43 targeted counties / designated areas of 15 more, or qualified military.

programs.name: Great Choice — Amortizing
programs.notes: 30-year amortizing second at the same rate as the first mortgage. Requires a THDA Great Choice first mortgage: FHA, USDA-RD or Freddie Mac HFA Advantage conventional; VA only via Homeownership for Heroes. First-time buyers, except repeat buyers in 43 targeted counties / designated areas of 15 more, or qualified military.

programs.name: Great Choice — new construction
programs.notes: 0% amortizing second for new or proposed construction, repaid over 15 years (THDA DPA page). Requires a Great Choice first mortgage.

programs.name: Homeownership for Heroes
programs.notes: Reduced Great Choice first-mortgage rate (FHA, USDA-RD or VA only) plus Great Choice Plus DPA (amount shown = amortizing option; the deferred $6k/$10k option is also available). Eligible: military/veterans, EMTs/paramedics, firefighters, full-time K-12 teachers and principals, law enforcement, public safety dispatchers. First-time requirement waived statewide for qualified military and veterans (others follow Great Choice rules).

Nashville.name: Tennessee Downpayment Partnership
Nashville.amountText: Amount not published by AHR; covers down payment and/or closing costs
Nashville.incomeNote: At or below 80% HUD AMI (Nashville-Davidson-Murfreesboro-Franklin MSA)
Nashville.notes: Due-on-sale loan, repaid only when the home is resold. First mortgage must come from a partner bank (First Community Bank, Studio Bank or Wilson Bank). Replaces NeighborhoodLIFT (a 2017 Wells Fargo one-time program, no longer offered). AHR does not state whether applications are currently open.

Memphis.name: Down Payment Assistance
Memphis.amountText: Current amount not published; FY23 city flyer: Citywide DPA up to 10% of price, max $10,000 (secondary guide cites up to $25,000)
Memphis.incomeNote: Citywide DPA up to 80% AMI; HIP Citizens up to 200% AMI in 15 designated areas; police/fire/MSCS incentives have no income limit
Memphis.source: City of Memphis program page (updated 2026-03-19) for sub-programs/income; FY23 City DPA flyer for terms
Memphis.notes: Deferred, no-payment second lien held 5 years and released if terms are met (FY23 flyer; listed as deferred conservatively). Minimum 1% buyer investment. Sub-programs: Citywide DPA, MHA DPA, HIP Citizens, HIP Police, HIP Fire, MSCS teachers. First-time rule applies to Citywide DPA (no ownership in 3 years); HIP variants only require owning no other property. Current dollar amounts could not be confirmed on the city site.

Chattanooga.name: CNE second loan
Chattanooga.notes: CNE in-house second mortgage at the same rate as the first mortgage, repaid monthly over at most 15 years, no prepayment penalty. CNE also lists a RockPointBank partner second of up to $50,000 (30-year amortization, Hamilton County, $1,000 minimum buyer contribution).
Chattanooga.incomeNote: Household income/size limits; southeast Tennessee service counties

Chattanooga.name: City of Chattanooga Down Payment Assistance
Chattanooga.amountText: Up to $15,000 (up to $21,000 combined with THDA)
Chattanooga.notes: 0% deferred subordinate loan, no monthly payments; forgiven in full (not prorated) after 30 years of owner occupancy; repaid on sale or cash-out refinance. City limits, price/appraisal max $400,000, $1,000 minimum buyer contribution, homebuyer education. First-time = no ownership in 3 years. Subject to fund availability. Credit 620 or first-mortgage minimum if higher. (30-year forgiveness and 620 credit from city guidelines page, not re-fetched 11/27; main page confirms amount, 0% deferred, first-time, income, price.)

Knoxville.name: Downpayment Assistance Program
Knoxville.agency: City of Knoxville Housing & Neighborhood Development
Knoxville.amountText: Amount not published on the city page
Knoxville.notes: Paused: the city says applications are closed except for homes developed by Home Source East Tennessee, Neighborhood Housing Inc. and East Tennessee Housing Development Corp. Terms not published; listed as deferred conservatively.

TX.name: Texas
TX.agency: TDHCA / Texas State Affordable Housing Corp. (TSAHC)

programs.name: My First Texas Home
programs.incomeNote: Income and purchase-price limits by county
programs.notes: 0% second lien, no payments, due on sale/refinance/payoff of first lien; a 3-year forgivable 2nd-lien option also exists. First-time = no ownership in 3 yrs (exceptions: targeted areas, qualified veterans). Homebuyer education required; program matrix dated 2/3/2025.

programs.name: My Choice Texas Home
programs.incomeNote: Income and purchase-price limits by county; separate options ≤80% AMI and >80% AMI
programs.notes: 0% second lien, no payments, due on sale/refinance/payoff of first lien; a 3-year forgivable 2nd-lien option also exists. Conventional = Fannie HFA Preferred / Freddie HFA Advantage; matrix dated 2/3/2025. Homebuyer education required.

programs.name: Home Sweet Texas Home Loan Program
programs.amountText: Up to 5% of loan (grant or 3-year forgivable second lien)
programs.incomeNote: Low/moderate income limits by county (up to ~80% / 150–170% AMI)
programs.notes: Offered as either a non-repayable grant or a second lien forgiven after 3 years; modeled conservatively as forgivable. Min credit 620 government / 640 conventional. Specific government loan types not named on the page. Purchase-price limits by county.

programs.name: Homes for Texas Heroes Home Loan Program
programs.amountText: Up to 5% of loan (grant or 3-year forgivable second lien)
programs.incomeNote: Income limits by county (up to ~80% / 150–170% AMI)
programs.notes: For teachers/K-12 staff, police, firefighters, EMS, corrections officers, nursing/allied health faculty and veterans. Grant or 3-yr forgivable option; modeled conservatively as forgivable. Min credit 620 government / 640 conventional.

Houston.name: Homebuyer Assistance Program (HAP)
Houston.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI (CDBG); up to 120% AMI for TIRZ-funded
Houston.notes: Closed to new applications: program funds exhausted (Nov 2026); reapply when funding is replenished. 0% forgivable junior lien: ≤$50,000 forgiven over 5 yrs, $50,000.01–$75,000 over 8 yrs (Guidelines v8.0). No minimum credit score; home must be taxed by City of Houston.

Harris County.name: Harris County Downpayment Assistance Program (DAP)
Harris County.incomeNote: Income-qualified; price ≤$285,000 existing / $296,000 new; unincorporated Harris County only
Harris County.notes: At capacity: currently accepting only Hurricane Beryl/Derecho-affected applicants. Silent second mortgage with 5-yr (<$25k) or 10-yr ($25k–$40k) affordability period; forgiveness not stated explicitly, so modeled as deferred. Loan types not listed by the county.

San Antonio.name: Homeownership Incentive Program (HIP 80)
San Antonio.notes: 0% no-payment second lien, forgiven over 5 years if ≤$15,000, 10 years if more. First lien must be FHA, VA or Conventional; no credit score required (Procedural Guide Oct 2024). Home within San Antonio city limits.

San Antonio.name: Homeownership Incentive Program (HIP 120)
San Antonio.notes: 0% no-payment second lien: 75% forgiven over 10 years, 25% perpetual (due on sale/refinance with cash out), so modeled as deferred. First-time (no ownership in 3 yrs); first lien FHA, VA or Conventional (Procedural Guide Oct 2024).

Dallas.name: Dallas Homebuyer Assistance Program (DHAP)
Dallas.agency: City of Dallas (administered by BCL of Texas)
Dallas.amountText: Up to $50,000; up to $60,000 in High Opportunity Areas
Dallas.notes: Administered by BCL of Texas since May 1, 2026. 0% forgivable deferred second lien prorated annually over the affordability term (term length not published). Funding first-come, first-served. Anti-Displacement DHAP (50–120% AMI, 10-yr Dallas residents) up to $50,000; Targeted Occupations DHAP funds fully spent. First-time rule, min credit and loan types not stated on agency pages.

Austin.name: Down Payment Assistance
Austin.agency: City of Austin Housing / Austin Housing Finance Corp.
Austin.notes: Standard DPA (≤$14,999) is a 0% loan forgiven after 5 years; shared-equity DPA ($15k–$40k) keeps a 30-year City equity interest, so modeled as deferred. The current City page confirms the $40,000 max, limits and first-time rule but not the split terms. No program credit minimum; loan types not specified; home in Austin full-purpose city limits.

Fort Worth.name: Homebuyer Assistance Program (HAP)
Fort Worth.agency: City of Fort Worth Neighborhood Services
Fort Worth.amountText: Up to $25,000 (deferred loan plus closing costs up to 3% of loan)
Fort Worth.notes: ≤$14,999 forgiven after 5 years; above that, 10-yr affordability (remainder forgiven 20%/yr in years 6–10). 30-yr fixed first mortgage from a city-approved lender; loan types not named. Subject to funding (guidelines rev. 4/15/2026).

Corpus Christi.name: Homebuyer Assistance Program
Corpus Christi.amountText: Up to $25,000 per household (per the City's Jan 2025 HOME notice); current terms unconfirmed. The previously cited $10,000 closing-cost add-on could not be confirmed
Corpus Christi.incomeNote: Low-income (HOME, ≤80% AMI); HOME rule caps price at 95% of area median purchase price. Earlier figure of ≤$238,000 not confirmed
Corpus Christi.notes: Paused: no open homebuyer application found on the City's site (rechecked 2026-11-27). The FY2026/PY2025 Annual Action Plan says Planning & Community Development runs a Homebuyer Down Payment and Closing Cost Assistance Program (CDBG program delivery $528,731; HOME Homebuyer and Builder Program $255,105 with Habitat for Humanity, 40–80% AMI) using HOME resale/recapture rules, but gives no per-household amount. The latest amount is from a Jan 2025 HOME notice (Come Dream Come Build, up to $25,000/family). The FY2027/PY2026 plan draft could not be read. Forgiveness not published, so modeled as deferred; confirm with the City (PCDD 361-826-3010).
Corpus Christi.source: City of Corpus Christi HOME Notice of Intent/RROF, Come Dream Come Build Homebuyer Assistance (Jan 8, 2025); FY2026/PY2025 Annual Action Plan draft

programs.name: UHC Down Payment Assistance
programs.amountText: Covers the minimum down payment (up to ~6%)
programs.notes: Traditional option: 30-year amortizing second at 1% above the first-mortgage rate. UHC now also offers a deferred-payment DPA. First-time and repeat buyers.

programs.name: First-Time Homebuyer New Construction
programs.notes: 0% loan from state funds (SB 240). Use for down payment, closing costs or a permanent rate buydown. 12 months Utah residency required; can stack with the UHC DPA second.

programs.name: First-Time Homebuyer Veterans Grant
programs.notes: State grant for veterans buying in Utah; funds appropriated by the Legislature and limited.

programs.name: Down Payment Assistance Grant
programs.notes: A true gift, never repaid. Down payment only. First-time buyers unless in a targeted area. Can’t be combined with the Plus Second or Closing Cost grant.

programs.name: Closing Cost Assistance Grant
programs.notes: Grant, never repaid, for buyers using a VA or USDA (RHS) loan.

programs.name: Virginia Housing Plus Second
programs.amountText: Covers the down payment (plus some closing costs)
programs.notes: 30-year fixed second mortgage, no prepayment penalty. First-time or repeat buyers, including those over the grant income limits.

programs.name: DHCD HOME Down Payment Assistance
programs.amountText: Up to 10% of price (15% in high-cost areas such as Arlington, Fairfax, Alexandria) plus up to $2,500 closing costs, max $40,000
programs.notes: 0% deferred loan with no payments that's fully forgiven at the end of the affordability period: 5 years for $1,000-$14,999, 10 years for $15,000-$40,000. Fixed-rate first mortgages only (no ARM/203k). Median FICO 620 and 3 trade lines. Buyer contribution is 1% of price (50-80% AMI) or $500 (<50% AMI). Delivered through regional local providers. Guidelines revised Oct 2024; separate pilot (≤60% AMI) offers up to $50,000.

Norfolk.name: NRHA HOME Program (HomeNet)
Norfolk.amountText: Up to $40,000 for down payment and closing costs
Norfolk.notes: Run by NRHA's HomeNet Homeownership Center. Forgiveness terms aren't published, so treated as deferred. Not owned a home in past 3 years, household income at least $25,000, no bankruptcy in past 2 years. Can be paired with Virginia Housing SPARC (1% rate reduction). Apply at homenetnorfolk.org; (757) 314-4202. Corrected from $60,000.

Norfolk.name: Homeward Norfolk
Norfolk.amountText: Up to $40,000 for down payment and closing costs
Norfolk.notes: Only for homes in Ingleside, Monticello Village and Oakdale Farms. Forgiveness terms not published, so treated as deferred. Through NRHA HomeNet, (757) 314-4202.

Virginia Beach.name: Workforce Housing Program
Virginia Beach.amountText: City second mortgage equal to a 1%-25% discount off the market value of a designated workforce unit
Virginia Beach.notes: The city's only published purchase-assistance program; no general city DPA is listed on vbgov.com. 0% second mortgage with no payments, repaid with a share of appreciation on resale or transfer. Only for designated workforce housing units. Must live or work full-time in Virginia Beach, own no other real estate, and have net worth no more than 50% of price. PAUSED: applicants go on a waiting list and units aren't guaranteed. Housing & Neighborhood Preservation, 757-385-5750.

Richmond.name: City of Richmond DPA (via HOME of Virginia)
Richmond.agency: Housing Opportunities Made Equal of Virginia (HOME)
Richmond.amountText: Amount set yearly by funder; HOME's programs range $7,500-$20,000 (city's current cap not published)
Richmond.notes: City-funded DPA administered by HOME. Usually not repaid if the buyer stays through the affordability period (typically 5 years, sometimes 10-15), but terms vary, so it's treated as deferred. Requires a buyer investment of at least $1,000 or 1% of price, no outstanding judgments or collections, and HOME counseling. HOME also runs Henrico, Chesterfield and state HOME-funded DPA in the region.

Fairfax County / Arlington.name: Fairfax County Down Payment Loan
Fairfax County / Arlington.agency: Fairfax County Dept. of Housing & Community Development
Fairfax County / Arlington.amountText: Amount not capped publicly (county example: $50,000 = 12.5% of a $400,000 price)
Fairfax County / Arlington.notes: Shared-equity deferred loan with no monthly payments. Repay the principal plus a share of net appreciation (loan / price) at payoff. Requires a Virginia Housing first mortgage from a prequalified lender; the county packet references conventional first trusts, and FHA/VA/USDA aren't mentioned. Can't be used for ADU/WDU units. First-time = no ownership in prior 3 years.

Fairfax County / Arlington.name: Moderate-Income Purchase Assistance Program (MIPAP)
Fairfax County / Arlington.notes: 0% deferred second mortgage with no payments, repaid on sale/refinance plus a share of net appreciation (capped at 25%). Conventional first mortgage from a Virginia Housing lender required. PAUSED: the county says MIPAP is NOT accepting applications at this time.

programs.name: ASSIST
programs.notes: 0% deferred loan, not forgiven — repaid at sale, refinance or payoff. True first-time buyers with under $20,000 in combined liquid assets; only with VHFA MOVE.

programs.name: NeighborWorks of Western VT DPA
programs.amountText: Up to $50,000 or 20% of price, whichever is lower
programs.notes: Second mortgage at 2 points above your first-mortgage rate, 15-year term; no PMI, no prepayment penalty. Homes anywhere in Vermont; apply through a NeighborWorks partner lender. Combines with VHFA ASSIST and Freddie Mac Home Possible Advantage. Income limits, first-time rule and first-mortgage types not stated on the page (loan types kept from prior data).

programs.name: First Generation Homebuyer Grant
programs.notes: No repayment. Parents or guardians must never have owned a home. Under $20,000 in liquid assets. Stacks with ASSIST for $25,000–$30,000 total; first come, first served.

Burlington.name: CHT Buyer Driven Shared Equity
Burlington.amountText: Up to $80,000 or 35% of price, whichever is less
Burlington.notes: Shared-equity grant: no repayment, but home stays permanently affordable and appreciation is shared at resale — treated as deferred (conservative). Price ≤$280,000; Chittenden County and nearby towns; income/asset eligibility certified by CHT; limited first-come funds.

programs.name: Home Advantage DPA
programs.amountText: 3%, 4% or 5% of loan (5% on FHA or conventional)
programs.notes: 0% deferred second paired with a Home Advantage first mortgage; repaid on sale, refinance, transfer, non-occupancy or payoff (at or before 30 years). No needs assessment for the 3–5% options. Homes under $250,000: see Needs-Based.

programs.name: Home Advantage Needs Based
programs.notes: 1% simple interest, no monthly payments; repaid on sale, refinance, transfer, non-occupancy or payoff (at or before 30 years). Needs assessment required (waived for veterans). Pairs with a Home Advantage first mortgage.

programs.name: House Key Opportunity DPA
programs.notes: 1% simple interest, payments deferred (due on sale/refinance/transfer or at 30 years). First-time buyers only unless purchasing in a Target Area. Needs assessment required (waived for veterans). Pairs with a House Key Opportunity first mortgage.
programs.incomeNote: King/Snohomish ≤ $93,350 (1–2 persons) / $116,650 (3+); Pierce/Clark/Kitsap/Skamania ≤ $83,000 / $103,700; lower in other counties

programs.name: Veterans DPA
programs.notes: 3% interest, payments deferred (due on sale/refinance/transfer or at 30 years). Honorably discharged veterans, WA National Guard/Reserve and certain surviving spouses/dependents. First-time buyers only unless purchasing in a Target Area.

programs.name: Covenant Homeownership Program
programs.amountText: Up to 20% of home cost, max $150,000, plus closing costs
programs.notes: For first-time buyers whose family lived in Washington before 1968 and was in a group harmed by housing discrimination. Repaid at sale or transfer; 2025 amendment (HB 1696) allows forgiveness for some participants. Waitlist: demand exceeds monthly funding — lenders must submit buyers for pre-reservation and buyers wait on a list until funds are available (the program still receives new funding monthly, so it is shown as active).

programs.name: HomeChoice DPA
programs.notes: For households where the buyer or a household member has a verified disability. Payment-deferred second (due on sale/refinance/transfer or at 30 years); interest rate not stated on the agency page. First-time buyers only unless purchasing in a Targeted Area. Needs assessment and one-on-one pre-purchase counseling required. Loan types follow the WSHFC first mortgage.

Seattle.name: Office of Housing DPA
Seattle.amountText: Up to $55,000 for open-market purchases; up to $70,000 (<3 bedrooms) / $90,000 (3+ bedrooms) for resale-restricted homes
Seattle.notes: City funds delivered through partners (e.g. HomeSight low-interest deferred loan, Homestead CLT resale-restricted homes). Home must be in Seattle city limits, price ≤ $450,000, owner-occupied; first-time (no ownership in 3 years); homebuyer education + counseling required. Interest/terms vary by partner — shown as deferred.

Tacoma.name: Down Payment Assistance
Tacoma.notes: 0% deferred 30-year loan for down payment/closing costs, Tacoma city limits; no ownership in prior 3 years. CLOSED: city page (updated 11/07/2025) says all funding is committed and applications are not being accepted.

East King County (ARCH).name: ARCH East King County DPA
East King County (ARCH).agency: A Regional Coalition for Housing (ARCH) / WSHFC
East King County (ARCH).notes: 4% simple interest, payments deferred (due on sale/refinance/transfer or at 30 years). Bellevue, Kirkland, Redmond, Issaquah, Sammamish, Bothell, Kenmore, Mercer Island, Newcastle, Woodinville and other East King cities (not Seattle). Price limits $646,000 existing / $660,000 new. Buyer contributes 2% of price (half may be gift). Pre-purchase counseling required. Loan types follow the WSHFC first mortgage.

programs.name: Easy Close DPA
programs.notes: Repaid monthly alongside the WHEDA Advantage first mortgage. Not limited to first-time buyers.

programs.name: Capital Access DPA
programs.notes: 0% deferred, due when the first mortgage is paid off or refinanced. For lower-income buyers in high-housing-need areas. Available again on a limited basis since Jan 15, 2026.

Madison.name: Home-Buy the American Dream
Madison.notes: Repaid with a share of appreciation at sale.

programs.name: Low Down Home Loan
programs.notes: 2% fixed, repaid over 15 years. Only with the Fund’s Homeownership (mostly first-time) or Movin’ Up programs; full $12,000 when loan-to-value is 80% or higher.

Charleston.name: Home Blend First-Time Homebuyer Program
Charleston.agency: City of Charleston Mayor's Office of Economic & Community Development (MOECD)
Charleston.amountText: Up to $28,000 ($26,000 down payment + $2,000 closing costs) per the City's 2022 brochure; current amount unconfirmed
Charleston.incomeNote: Low/moderate income (HOME, ≤80% AMI); 2022 limits $37,200 (1) to $57,350 (5). Home in City of Charleston or Kanawha County
Charleston.notes: HOME-funded assistance from MOECD paired with a participating-lender first mortgage; buyer must contribute at least $500. 2022 brochure calls it a forgivable loan but gives no forgiveness schedule, so modeled conservatively as deferred. No home owned in past 3 years. The FY2026 Action Plan (draft Apr 29, 2026) still funds HOME first-time homebuyer down payment/closing cost help (~$494,000 for 15 households) but gives no per-household amount. No current program page found; loan types not stated. Confirm with MOECD (304-348-8035).
Charleston.source: City of Charleston Home Blend brochure (2022) and Draft FY2026 Annual Action Plan (Apr 2026), charlestonwv.gov

programs.name: Home$tretch DPA
programs.notes: 0% loan, no monthly payments; due at sale, refinance or 30-year maturity. Covers down payment, closing costs and prepaids. Pairs only with WCDA First-Time Homebuyer, Spruce Up or Edge loans; first-time rule (no ownership in 3 years) applies with First-Time Homebuyer and Spruce Up, not Edge. $1,500 minimum borrower contribution (may be a gift).

programs.name: Amortizing DPA
